sections.label: GST and NIRC decisions
sections.summary: A speech said the Government's decisions to raise GST to 9% and not raise the NIRC above 50% are justified as pragmatic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It may be useful to outline her speech first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: She said the Government's decision to increase the Goods and Services Tax (GST) to 9% is justified as a pragmatic decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: She said the Government's decision not to raise the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) to above the 50% mark is also justified as a pragmatic decision.

sections.label: GST increase next term
sections.summary: The GST is proposed to be increased in the next term of Government after carefully studying all other options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The GST is proposed to be increased in the next term of Government after carefully studying all other options.

sections.label: Borrowings secured by guarantee
sections.summary: Borrowings for infrastructural developments are to be secured by guarantee, subject to the President's approval, secured by the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Borrowings for infrastructural developments are to be secured by guarantee, subject to the President's approval, which, in turn, is secured by the Reserves.

sections.label: Programme spending estimates
sections.summary: Based on estimates, the Government would have committed up to $7.2 billion, with amounts given for 2013-2015, 2016-2017 and the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Based on estimates, the Government would have committed up to $7.2 billion for this programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For the period 2013 to 2015, it is about $3.6 billion; 2016 to 2017, it is $1.8 billion; and an additional $1.8 billion for the next three years.

sections.label: 2017 productivity and unemployment
sections.summary: Productivity growth for 2017 is 4.5%, highest since 2010, and citizen unemployment stands at 3.3% based on MOM preliminary figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Productivity growth for 2017 is 4.5%, highest since 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Citizen unemployment rate for 2017, based on the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) preliminary figures, stands at 3.3%, better than in 2013 when it was 2.9%.

sections.label: Charity donations and casino levies
sections.summary: Donations rose from $2 billion in 2011 to $2.7 billion in 2017, and raising the casino entry levy will protect Singaporeans and PRs and support charities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: On the aspect of financial support for charities, I note that the total donations have increased from $2 billion in 2011 to $2.7 billion in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In financial year (FY) 2016/2017, Tote Board approved disbursements of $459 million to these sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the past five financial years beginning from 2012, Tote Board collected an average of about $150 million from casino entry levies per year, which is used to fund its grant-making activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Increasing the casino entry levy will enhance the safeguard to protect Singaporeans and Permanent Residents (PRs) from the ill-effects of gambling and, at the same time, allow charities to be better supported through Tote Board’s grant-making activities.

sections.label: FDI stock and reserves
sections.summary: Singapore's 2016 FDI stock was S$1.4 trillion, and a 30% outflow would wipe out S$400 billion, while MAS official foreign reserves are $370 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: For example, to put things in perspective, based on 2016 data, Singapore's foreign direct investment (FDI) stock is S$1.4 trillion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: If there is a loss of confidence or catastrophe and, let us say, 30% only of the FDIs were to move out, it will wipe out S$400 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: And we should note that the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS') official foreign reserves are only $370 billion, and this is just 30% of the FDIs. "FDI", if I may define it, is actually the amount of investments by foreign multinational companies (MNCs) or multinational enterprises investing in Singapore.

sections.label: Future generations bearing infrastructure costs
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Minister for Finance's assurance that future generations should partly bear financial responsibility for infrastructure built for future needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: That is an important point I want to share today from that perspective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: I am glad also with the Minister for Finance's assurance in his speech that we need to take the right approach to have future generations in part bear financial responsibility for infrastructure projects that are built for future needs.

sections.label: Possible deferral of GST hike
sections.summary: If this is achievable, there could be a chance for the proposed GST hike to be deferred to a later date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: If this is achievable, then perhaps there could be a chance for the proposed GST hike to be deferred to a later date.

sections.label: Borrowing for infrastructure and contingent liability
sections.summary: Borrowing by Statutory Boards and Government-owned companies for infrastructure is one funding solution, but contingent liability must be considered given unpredictable global economy and financial markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: As mentioned in the Budget speech, borrowing arrangements for Statutory Boards and Government-owned companies which build infrastructure would form one part of the solution for funding large investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: However, contingent liability is a potential future issue that must be taken into account, given the unpredictable nature of the global economy and the financial markets.

sections.label: Concern over ITE education spending
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned that decision points and tradeoffs may reduce spending on education and skills training, particularly for the ITE segment, about 25% of the post-secondary cohort yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: I am concerned if some of the decision points and tradeoffs may lead to reduced spending in specific areas of education and skills training, in particular, the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) segment of the student population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: They constitute about 25% of the post-secondary cohort each year and are a significant future labour force with key skillsets for us to be future-ready.

sections.label: ITE Work-Learn Technical Diploma
sections.summary: ITE has advanced by providing new upgrading pathways for alumni and in-service workers through the Work-Learn Technical Diploma, an apprenticeship path to higher certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Recently, ITE had made further advancement by providing new upgrading pathways for its alumni and in-service workers through the programme called Work-Learn Technical Diploma (WLTD), which is a path towards higher certification through apprenticeship model.

sections.label: Support for ITE programmes
sections.summary: The speaker says programmes like ITE WLTD and GEP have been life-changing and hopes support and development resources for ITE continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: It has proven to be life-changing for some of the students and is impactful, especially for those who come from humble backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: So, I hope the Government will ensure that the support for programmes like those in ITE and, for example, programmes like the ITE WLTD and GEP, will not be affected, and future demands for development resources will continue to be given to ITE.

sections.label: ITE students financial assistance
sections.summary: Over 50% of ITE students qualify for financial assistance, and the speaker hopes budget growth reductions do not cut ITE Opportunity Funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: More than 50% of ITE students qualify for some form of financial assistance and they generally come from diverse challenging backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: So, the ITE schemes allow more direct assistance to the students and their families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: I do hope that tradeoffs from the reduction in the budget growth do not lead to reductions in the ITE Opportunity Funds, for example.

sections.label: Limiting Ministries' budget growth
sections.summary: The Minister says he will keep his response to about 30% of 10 hours, in line with limiting Ministries' budget growth to 30% of GDP growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As you said, over 50 Members have spoken for more than 10 hours, and if I were to do a point-to-point discussion, it will take us beyond 10.00 pm tonight.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, in line with my Ministry's policy of limiting Ministries' budget growth to 30% of gross domestic product (GDP) growth, I shall try to keep it to about 30% of 10 hours.

sections.label: Rise in healthcare spending
sections.summary: Government healthcare spending is projected to rise from 2.2% of GDP to around 3% in the next decade, $3.6 billion more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Government healthcare spending is projected to rise by nearly 0.8 percentage points of GDP from 2.2% of GDP today to around 3% in the next decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: That is $3.6 billion more in today’s dollars.

sections.label: Doubling of seniors by 2030
sections.summary: From now till 2030, the number of seniors will double from about 450,000 to 900,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: From now till 2030, the number of seniors will double from about 450,000 to 900,000.

sections.label: Doubling of preschool spending
sections.summary: Preschool spending is expected to double in the next five years to $1.7 billion a year in 2022, up about 0.1 percentage point of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Preschool spending is expected to double in the next five years to $1.7 billion a year in 2022, an increase of about 0.1 percentage point of GDP from today.

sections.label: Spending outcomes and GDP share
sections.summary: Passage states outcomes depend on how well money is spent, with FY2018 expenditure about 19% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Indeed, as Miss Cheryl Chan has noted, it is not about how much we spend, but how well we spend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We achieve very credible outcomes, with overall expenditures of about 19% of GDP in FY2018.

sections.label: Singapore healthcare and policing outcomes
sections.summary: Singapore spends less on healthcare yet has high healthy life expectancy, and ranked top in the 2017 Gallup Global Law and Order Index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Compared to other countries shown on this chart, Singapore spends less on healthcare, yet achieves a high healthy life expectancy, higher than the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Similarly, we are able to get effective outcomes for our spending on policing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We were ranked top in the 2017 Gallup Global Law and Order Index, which gauges people’s sense of personal security and their experiences with crime and law enforcement when living in their respective jurisdictions.

sections.label: FY2017 surplus one-off factors
sections.summary: The FY2017 surplus was largely due to one-off, exceptional factors not expected every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The surplus in FY2017 was largely due to one-off, exceptional factors that we do not expect to occur every year.

sections.label: Reserving FY2017 surplus for future needs
sections.summary: The bulk of the FY2017 surplus is reserved for future needs like MRT development plans and ElderShield subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We should not plan for our future in the hope that markets will always continue to move in Singapore’s favour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: That is why we are reserving the bulk of the FY2017 surplus for future needs like the Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) development plans and ElderShield subsidies.

sections.label: GST increase timing decision
sections.summary: Careful assessment led to the determination that GST must be raised sometime between 2021 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We assess carefully what we need to do in response and how we should find the resources to support our plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This is how we had determined that we will need to raise GST sometime in the period from 2021 to 2025.

sections.label: GST increase and expenditure needs
sections.summary: A two-percentage point GST increase raises about 0.7% of GDP yearly, not fully covering expenditure needs but making the fiscal gap more manageable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As mentioned, a two-percentage point increase in GST rate is expected to raise revenues worth about 0.7% of GDP per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: On the other hand, the expenditure drivers that I earlier mentioned – healthcare, security and preschools – already exceed this amount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: These are serious commitments that we must budget for, and there are risks that overall spending could rise further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: So, the two-percentage point GST increase will not fully cover our expenditure needs, but only make the fiscal gap more manageable, in conjunction with other measures to manage expenditure.

sections.label: Benefits versus taxes by income
sections.summary: The middle-income group receives $2 in benefits per dollar of tax paid, and the lower-income group about $4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The middle-income group gets $2 in benefits for every dollar of tax that they pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The lower-income group gets about $4 in benefits for every dollar of tax.

sections.label: Raising personal income tax progressivity
sections.summary: PIT was raised in recent years, with higher marginal rates for chargeable income above $160,000 and a top rate of 22% above $320,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have raised PIT in recent years to further enhance progressivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We increased the marginal tax rates for higher-income earners with chargeable income exceeding $160,000 and raised the top marginal rate from 20% to 22% for those with chargeable income exceeding $320,000.

sections.label: Property tax and stamp duty collections
sections.summary: About $8 billion was collected on average in recent years from property tax and stamp duty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: On average, we collected about $8 billion in recent years from property tax and stamp duty.

sections.label: Estimated additional revenue from measure
sections.summary: In reply to Mr Pritam Singh, the estimate is additional revenue of about $90 million per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh asked if this will yield additional revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We estimate it could yield additional revenue of about $90 million per year.

sections.label: 2017 investment commitments and jobs
sections.summary: In 2017, $9.4 billion of fixed asset investments and $6.5 billion of total business expenditure were committed, creating about 22,500 jobs when fully implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In 2017, $9.4 billion of fixed asset investments and $6.5 billion of total business expenditure were committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: When the projects are fully implemented, about 22,500 jobs will be created.

sections.label: NIRC share for budgetary needs
sections.summary: From the returns, 50% is taken as NIRC to supplement budgetary needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: From the returns, we take 50% as NIRC to supplement our budgetary needs.

sections.label: NIRC framework and spending cap
sections.summary: Without the NIRC framework, PIT or GST collections would have had to double to raise the same revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: If we did not introduce the NIRC framework, we would have had to double our PIT collection or our GST collection to raise the same amount of revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And yet, some have suggested increasing the NIRC spending cap from the current 50% to 60% or using a portion of land sales proceeds for recurrent social spending.

sections.label: Reserves rules and NIRC cap
sections.summary: Rules on land sales and the 50% NIRC cap were introduced to avoid drawing more from Reserves for current expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The rules on Reserves were debated and agreed in this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We deliberately introduced rules on land sales and the 50% NIRC cap so that we do not succumb to the temptation to draw more from our Reserves to fund current expenditure or eat into the principal sum.

sections.label: US and EU unemployment recovery
sections.summary: The US unemployment rate recovered to pre-Global Financial Crisis levels only last year, and some EU rates have not recovered after 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For example, the US unemployment rate only recovered to pre-Global Financial Crisis levels last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Unemployment rates in some European Union (EU) countries have not recovered even after 10 years.

sections.label: GST on imported services yield
sections.summary: The yield from GST on imported services is small, less than $100 million, and none of the alternatives to a GST increase is viable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: He asked if we can rely on GST on imported services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I have explained that the yield is small, less than $100 million, and that we need to do this to protect our revenue base.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Any serious-minded person will appreciate that not one of these is a viable alternative to a GST increase.

sections.label: Carbon tax and business support
sections.summary: A carbon tax at $5 per tonne of emissions runs from 2019 to 2023, with funds set aside to help businesses improve energy efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: With the introduction of a carbon tax at an initial rate of $5 per tonne of emissions from 2019 to 2023, we join many countries that have done the same to step up global efforts to address climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked about helping businesses to reduce carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will set aside funds from 2019 to 2023 to support them in improving energy efficiency.

sections.label: ASEAN opportunities and market size
sections.summary: ASEAN presents great opportunities, with over 640 million people and a GDP of over US$2.5 trillion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As Mr Henry Kwek pointed out, ASEAN presents great opportunities, with over 640 million people and a GDP of over US$2.5 trillion.

sections.label: SBF National Business Survey
sections.summary: In the SBF National Business Survey, nearly three in four companies reported introducing new processes or training to improve efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In the recent Singapore Business Federation (SBF) National Business Survey, nearly three in four companies reported that they introduced new processes or training to improve efficiency.

sections.label: Local startup investment 2017
sections.summary: In 2017, about US$1.4 billion was invested in the local startup scene, over 10 times the amount five years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In 2017, about US$1.4 billion (S$1.85 billion) was invested in the local startup scene, more than 10 times the amount invested five years ago.

sections.label: Singapore Bloomberg Innovation Index ranking
sections.summary: Singapore climbed three places in the Bloomberg Innovation Index to rank third most innovative economy globally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Internationally, people are paying attention to the increasingly vibrant innovation scene in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This year, Singapore climbed three places in the Bloomberg Innovation Index to become ranked as the third most innovative economy globally.

sections.label: Professional Conversion Programmes placements
sections.summary: Placements through Professional Conversion Programmes in 2017 were about 3,700, more than double the 2016 placements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The number of placements through Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) in 2017 is about 3,700, more than double the placements in 2016.

sections.label: MOM accepts workgroup recommendations
sections.summary: MOM has accepted the recommendations in the workgroup's report released last week and will elaborate on strategies at COS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: MOM has accepted the recommendations in the workgroup’s report which was released last week, and will further elaborate on their strategies at COS.

sections.label: Support for older workers
sections.summary: For older workers, employability is supported through the Special Employment Credit and Adapt and Grow programmes, and training through SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For older workers, we support their employability through the Special Employment Credit and Adapt and Grow programmes, and their training through SkillsFuture.

sections.label: Calibrated foreign worker inflow
sections.summary: It states a need to allow a calibrated inflow of foreign workers, especially in areas of critical shortages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: At the same time, we need to allow for a calibrated inflow of foreign workers, especially in areas of critical shortages.

sections.label: OECD PISA study finding
sections.summary: The OECD PISA study found about half of 15-year-old Singapore students from the lowest socioeconomic quarter performed in the top quarter globally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The OECD PISA study found that about half of the 15-year-old Singapore students from the lowest quarter by socioeconomic status performed in the top quarter of students in all countries, after accounting for socioeconomic status.

sections.label: Post-secondary progression by cohort
sections.summary: For students in the lowest 20% of households, half of the 1985 Primary 1 cohort reached post-secondary education, rising to nine in 10 for 2000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For students in the lowest 20% of households by socioeconomic status, half of them in the 1985 Primary 1 cohort progressed to post-secondary education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And this rose to nine in 10 for the 2000 Primary 1 cohort.

sections.label: MOF social mobility papers
sections.summary: MOF released occasional papers in 2012 and 2015 on social mobility, finding cohorts from 1969 to 1982 experienced good social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: MOF released two occasional papers in 2012 and 2015 on social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We found that cohorts from 1969 to 1982 have, indeed, experienced good social mobility.

sections.label: Support for VWOs
sections.summary: It recognises VWOs' contributions and encourages more support through 250% tax deduction for IPC donations, matching grants and BIPS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Many Members, such as Dr Lily Neo and Ms Chia Yong Yong, spoke of the good work that our VWOs do in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We recognise the invaluable contributions they make and are encouraging more support for them, through the 250% tax deduction for donations made to Institutions of a Public Character (IPCs), matching grants for donations raised, and the Business and IPC Partnership Scheme (BIPS).

sections.label: Consolidating senior-related services
sections.summary: Consolidating senior-related services under AIC and strengthening social service delivery through SSOs will enable better care for seniors and vulnerable families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The consolidation of senior-related services under the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), and the continuing efforts to strengthen social service delivery through our Social Service Offices (SSOs) will enable us to do more with the resources we have, and better care for our seniors and vulnerable families.

sections.label: Support for economic and fiscal measures
sections.summary: Members supported measures to position the economy for the future, foster a cohesive society, and provide for longer-term fiscal needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Members have expressed support for measures to position our economy for the future, so that Singaporeans will have opportunities to pursue their aspirations, regardless of where they start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have supported moves to foster a more cohesive and caring society so that we can better care for our elderly and the vulnerable amongst us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And there has been broad support for the fiscal measures to provide for our longer-term needs.

sections.label: Working together as a country
sections.summary: Working together made Singapore one of the healthiest, best educated and safest countries while keeping spending low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We can only make it through this journey, if we work together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: It is by working together, that we have become one of the healthiest, best educated and safest countries in the world, while keeping our spending low.

sections.label: Party position on GST announcement
sections.summary: A clarification is sought on the Party position and why Mr Pritam Singh said it cannot support the announcement at this point.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second clarification is about the Party position on the announcement of the GST – and I think Mr Pritam Singh may also elaborate on this further – about why it was said by him that we cannot support the announcement at this point in time.

sections.label: Supporting Budget but not GST hike
sections.summary: The intention is to support the Budget when the vote is called, but this is not support for a possible GST hike in a later Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Related to that, I should clarify, in case anybody misunderstands, that it is our intention to support the Budget when the vote is called but this should not be mistaken as a support for this announcement of some possible GST hike in a later Budget.

sections.label: Land sales and lease returns
sections.summary: Land sales include many leases which come back to the Government after the tenure of the lease.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Land sales actually include many leases which do come back to the Government after the tenure of the lease.

sections.label: Equity gap between poorer and richer students
sections.summary: A Parliamentary Question was filed before, and the report highlights that poorer students are further behind richer students domestically compared to OECD countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have filed a Parliamentary Question on this before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But I think the report also highlights that as far as equity is concerned, our poorer students seem to be further behind our richer students − the gap internally, domestically − compared to the OECD countries.

sections.label: GST increase and spending needs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Member accepts the need to spend more, and says a two-percentage point GST increase does not fully cover expected healthcare expenditure growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Does the Member accept, first and foremost, all that we said, that we do need to spend more, whether it is preschool, whether it is SkillsFuture, whether it is healthcare, whether it is revamping the economy, whether it is security?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And if it is, as I said, very clearly, in today's debate, in my round up, I said that even the two-percentage point increase in GST does not fully cover the expected increase in healthcare expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Can we take one measure first, and look at how we can meet that?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: So, Mr Pritam Singh's argument about "I can't support this at this point because it is so far away, I don't know your revenue pattern, I don't know your spending pattern and, therefore, I don't know what you can do and, therefore, I'm not going to support it." I do not think it is a rigorous or an honest position.

sections.label: Knowing everything before deciding
sections.summary: The speaker says requiring knowledge of every expenditure item before deciding would have led to serious deficit long ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I mean that, that is very simple to understand and I really do not understand why you want to create this… or I must know everything before I can decide on anything.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I think if I had taken that approach, if previous Finance Ministers had taken that approach, that I must know every item of expenditure before I can support you, before I know how much to raise, we would have been in serious deficit long, long ago.

sections.label: Cost and funding of proposals
sections.summary: The speaker asks how much the proposals will cost, where the money will come from, and whether a two-percentage point increase would help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And if you do, then tell me how much is it going to cost?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And even to fund a fraction of what you have suggested, where is the money going to come from, and would a two-percentage point increase help us in some ways?

sections.label: Land sales proceeds over lease
sections.summary: The speaker says land sales are mostly long leases, so proceeds should be considered over their lifespan, and taking 20% is not proper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The basic fact is this: most of our land sales are of pretty long leases − 99 years; for industrial land, some 30 years, some 60 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: If you are rigorous about it, you really ought to be spending no more than 1% of that land sale proceeds even if you want to use land sales proceeds because that is what the land is worth for a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: But for Mr Pritam Singh to say, "Oh, don't worry, let's take 20% of the land sales and, therefore, use that", is it not the equivalent?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And you are not going to get the land back over the length of the lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: So, that stream, that upfront capital payment, ought to be considered over its lifespan and, therefore, it is not proper.

sections.label: Government reliance on Reserves
sections.summary: The speaker states the Government's reliance on Reserves quadrupled from 2006 to 2011, from about $2 billion to about $8 billion, and has since doubled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Just as a matter of perspective on the question of using our Reserves as a source of income, the Government's reliance on Reserves has quadrupled from 2006 to 2011, from about $2 billion to about $8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since then, to the upcoming financial year, it has doubled from that.

sections.label: Temasek inclusion in NIRC
sections.summary: The speaker says Finance Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam stated Temasek's inclusion in the NIRC framework would raise NIRC's share of GDP from 2% to about 3% on average over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, in his Second Reading speech, when the Constitution was amended in 2015 to include Temasek in the NIRC framework, Finance Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam said that Temasek's inclusion would increase the NIRC’s share of GDP from 2% to about 3% on average over five years.

sections.label: NIRC NII NIR breakdown
sections.summary: A Member asks how much of the $15.8 billion NIRC came from NII and NIR, and the NIRC is said to be doubling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The third question is with reference to the NIRC portion of this year's Budget: how much in dollar terms of the $15.8 billion originated from the Net Investment Income (NII) component of NIRC, and NIR component respectively?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Member's first question, about the fact that our NIRC is, in fact, becoming an increasing source of revenue for the Government: that is correct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This number has been doubling; from $2 billion to $8 billion to $16 billion that the Member mentioned.

sections.label: NIR formula smoothens fluctuations
sections.summary: Building finances on short-term fluctuations is not sound, so the NIR formula has a built-in way to smoothen asset fluctuations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And it is not sound to build our finances on short-term fluctuations, whether up or down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: That is why the NIR formula has a built-in way to smoothen these asset fluctuations.

sections.label: Reserves Management Committee allocation
sections.summary: A whole-of-Government Reserves Management Committee chaired by the Prime Minister allocates land sales proceeds to entities for long-term gains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Member asked about how the land sales proceeds get to MAS, GIC and Temasek, and how do we divide that?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have a whole-of-Government Reserves Management Committee chaired by the Prime Minister and there we look at the risks and returns of different entities, the risks and returns across the different markets and allocate it for long-term gains, taking into account both the returns as well as the risks at the current market environment.

sections.label: Reserves beyond Singapore dollar
sections.summary: The Reserves are not just about maintaining the strength of the Singapore dollar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Reserves are not just about maintaining the strength of the Singapore dollar.

sections.label: Reserves crisis role
sections.summary: The Reserves play a crisis role tested in the Asian Financial Crisis, and longer-term assets can be mobilised if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In terms of maintaining the strength of the Singapore dollar, the Reserves play a very important crisis role which was what was tested during the Asian Financial Crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: One, our finances are sound; that our fiscal policy at the various stages of the crisis is sound.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And that is why I mentioned that we are one of 11 countries with a triple-A credit rating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Two, speculators know that should they try to attack the Singapore dollar, it is not just our official reserves that they have to contend with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We also have reserves that are invested in longer-term assets and that we will be able to mobilise, if we need to.

sections.label: Funds and future taxes
sections.summary: The Member argues that Government positions show no money is needed this term and taxes will need to be raised for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If one, with some commonsense, puts those facts together with another set of facts, which is that Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam and the Prime Minister had said that the Government had enough funds for this term, if you put those two sets of Government positions together, is it not absolutely clear that (a) we do not need money for this term, and (b) we will need to raise taxes for the future?

sections.label: Government budgeting and GST increase
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether Ms Lim will withdraw the claim that the Government behaved dishonestly, citing conservative budgeting and the Finance Minister's contingency warnings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: One can look at the principles that our Government uses for budgeting, which are usually very conservative, and we also have heard the Finance Minister talk about the fact that we must be prepared for all contingencies, so, if those announcements had not been made, we may be facing a GST increase in this Budget Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Seeing what the facts are, as I have set them out, would Ms Lim agree that the suggestions are baseless, and are you prepared to withdraw that this Government behaved dishonestly?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I said that the Government is stuck with the announcement that they have enough money for the decade.

sections.label: No Latin translators, PAP MPs rumours
sections.summary: The speaker says there are no Latin translators and recalls that PAP MPs were encouraged to bring even rumours to the House for refutation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Unfortunately, we do not have translators for Latin.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: And if I recall earlier debates, even People's Action Party (PAP) MPs were encouraged to come to the House to convey even rumours, so that the Government has the opportunity to refute them.

sections.label: Finance Minister confirms revenue statement
sections.summary: The speaker presents himself as a witness and confirms Deputy Prime Minister Tharman's statement that revenues are enough till this term of Government is accurate and truthful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I want to present myself as your witness, because I have been working on this ever since I became Finance Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I want to confirm that the statement made by Deputy Prime Minister Tharman: that we have enough revenues till this term of Government, is correct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have done all our projections and that is an accurate and truthful statement.

sections.label: Honest assessment, no GST increase now
sections.summary: The speaker says the assessment of the position between 2021 and 2025 remains accurate, which is why no GST increase was needed in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: If, indeed, we were so short, would it not be the logical thing to say, "Let's do it now" and find some ways to do it?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I said that it is between 2021 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: It is an honest assessment of our position, which remains accurate till today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: That is why I did not have to do a GST increase now, in this Budget.

sections.label: Reserves numbers as strategic asset
sections.summary: The speaker says Ms Kuik understands the need for Reserves numbers not to be revealed because they serve as a strategic asset.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As to the second question, Ms Kuik understands the need for our Reserves numbers not to be revealed because it serves as a strategic asset.

sections.label: MAS official foreign reserves in data
sections.summary: The speaker states that the MAS' official foreign reserves are actually in the data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Two, the MAS' official foreign reserves are actually in the data.

sections.label: Support for Budget measures
sections.summary: The speaker says they support this Budget as far as its measures go.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Yes, Sir, I thought I made it clear earlier that we support this Budget, as far as the measures in the Budget go.

sections.label: Voting results declared
sections.summary: The voting results are declared as 89 Ayes, eight Noes and zero Abstentions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will proceed to declare the voting results now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are 89 "Ayes", eight "Noes", and zero "Abstentions".

sections.label: GST increase and fiscal sustainability
sections.summary: The GST increase, at least three years away, is meant for future spending increases beyond 2020, not a deferred tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believe we can do more on this front.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But among the most talked about aspect in this year’s Budget is, of course, the topic of fiscal sustainability and the two-percentage point increase in GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The timing of the GST increase, at least three years from now, should not come as a surprise as both the current and previous Ministers for Finance have already made it quite clear that we do have sufficient revenue to meet the increased expenditures for this term of Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, this increase in GST is not a deferred tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is meant to take care of future spending increases beyond 2020.

sections.label: Moody's estimate of Qatari injection
sections.summary: Moody's estimates the Qatari government injected almost US$40 billion in the crisis's first couple of months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to estimates by the ratings agency Moody’s, the Qatari government injected almost US$40 billion into the economy, just in the first couple of months of the crisis.

sections.label: Reserves investment returns balancing Budgets
sections.summary: Investment returns on reserves provide about $14.6 billion in FY2017, and past NIR and NII contributions exceed $100 billion over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Perhaps, what is even more tangible is that the reserves that our forefathers have painstakingly built up over the decades have generated investment returns, and 50% of it is today the largest contributing revenue helping to balance our annual Budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This amounts to about $14.6 billion in FY2017, which is actually an expansionary injection to the economy, as it is not taken in through tax leakages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years, the Net Investment Returns (NIR) – previously the Net Investment Income (NII) – contributions of past Budgets have added up to more than $100 billion.

sections.label: Surpluses topping up endowment funds
sections.summary: Government surpluses top up endowment funds like ComCare, Pioneer Generation Package and the GSTV Fund to help Singaporeans after 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Government has also used surpluses from each term of Government to top up endowment funds like ComCare, Pioneer Generation Package and, in this year's Budget, a further top-up to the GSTV Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is to accumulate resources so that we can help more Singaporeans when the GST increase comes into effect after 2021.

sections.label: Funding recurrent spending with taxation
sections.summary: The passage says recurrent spending like healthcare and security should be funded by current taxation so each generation pays its share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This would give Singaporeans a sense that everyone has a stake in this country and we are all aligned to work together for the betterment of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This year’s Budget also sets out with great clarity the framework principles on how the Government would fund various spending and how, for some of the infrastructure projects, the share of funding can be distributed more equitably across generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I agree with the Minister for Finance that, for recurrent spending like healthcare, security and other social expenditures where it directly benefits the current generation, they should be funded with current taxation so that every generation pays its share.

sections.label: Funding long-term infrastructure projects
sections.summary: For long-term mega infrastructure projects, the Government will set aside surpluses and use accumulated savings to pay part of lumpy investment costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For the longer term mega infrastructure projects with high capital investments, the Government will set aside surpluses where possible, and to use savings accumulated to pay part of the lumpy investment costs.

sections.label: IPS survey on reserves and taxation
sections.summary: A recent Institute of Policy Studies survey suggests Singaporeans have an almost equal split view on using reserves or taxation for social spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A recent Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) survey with regard to the use of reserves or taxation to pay for social spending suggests that Singaporeans do have an almost equal split view on this issue.

sections.label: Last year's Budget surplus and GST
sections.summary: Last year's Budget had a $9.6 billion surplus, $700 million went to SG Bonus, and the Finance Minister prescribed a coming GST hike.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Last year’s Budget recorded a healthy surplus of $9.6 billion, thanks to exceptional items.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Seven hundred million dollars was set aside to share with Singaporeans via SG Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: When looking beyond short-term headline numbers into the longer-term outlook, Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat prescribed the bitter pill of a GST hike to come.

sections.label: Raising gambling tax rates
sections.summary: Bringing Singapore's gambling tax rates closer to Macau's and Australia's could collect much of the $3 billion intended from a GST hike.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: By bringing Singapore's low gambling tax rates of 5% to 15% closer in line with Macau's rate of 39% and Australia’s rate of up to 45% in some states, the authorities can collect much of the $3 billion intended to be drawn from a two-percentage point GST hike.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme impact
sections.summary: The impact of the $4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme announced in Budget 2016 has yet to be realised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, the impact of the $4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme announced in Budget 2016 has yet to be realised.

sections.label: Foreign manpower policy adjustments
sections.summary: The Budget does not address the shrinking workforce or foreign manpower policy, and the speaker calls for adjustments to foreign manpower to support growth areas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Third, the Budget does not address measures to deal with Singapore’s shrinking workforce nor offer guidance on foreign manpower policy, despite calls for help by businesses struggling to deal with manpower shortages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: While we must continue our manpower-lean approach as the way for firms to grow and maintain the overall ratio of local-to-foreign talents in our workforce, I call on the Government to consider some adjustments to the mix of foreign manpower to support growth areas earmarked in the future economy, such as expertise in data analytics, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In order to capitalise on the growth momentum, foreign manpower policies may need to evolve to include skill-based factors to prioritise types of foreign skills and expertise, like those adopted in other countries.

sections.label: Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty tier
sections.summary: The speaker suggested an additional tier of Buyer's Stamp Duty for properties with transaction values above S$1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In particular, I suggested having an additional tier of Buyer's Stamp Duty for properties with transaction values above S$1 million.

sections.label: Second foreign domestic worker levy
sections.summary: The levy for a second FDW rose from $265 to $450, while the concessionary rate of $60 a month for families needing care help remains unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In particular, the levy for a second FDW has increased from $265 to $450, representing almost a 70% increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But I am sure households which can afford to hire two or more FDWs would be able to afford the increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I wish to reiterate that families who may need help in caring for young children, the elderly, or family members with disabilities will not be affected by this increase as they will continue to enjoy the concessionary levy rate of $60 a month which remains unchanged.

sections.label: Wine duty by bottle price
sections.summary: Under the current system, a $50 bottle of wine is charged the same duty as one costing more than $1,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the current system, a bottle of wine which costs $50 is charged the same duty as another bottle which costs more than $1,000.

sections.label: Workers' Party on Budget
sections.summary: The Workers' Party notes that this year's Budget seeks to prepare Singapore and establish strong foundations for economic growth for the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers’ Party notes that this year’s Budget is one that seeks to prepare Singapore and establish strong foundations for economic growth for the next 10 years.

sections.label: Learning landscape design review
sections.summary: The Minister for Education in charge of Higher Education said the Government is examining how to better design the learning landscape, but this may take a generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Only last month, the Minister for Education in charge of Higher Education shared that the Government is examining how it can better design the learning landscape so as to ensure that opportunities are available for Singaporeans to succeed in life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the Minister said that this endeavour may take a generation.

sections.label: Singapore tuition culture industry
sections.summary: The passage states that a tuition culture continues in Singapore and is alleged to be a billion-dollar industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, we continue to have a tuition culture which is alleged to be a billion-dollar industry in Singapore.

sections.label: Streaming and ranking reinforce inequality
sections.summary: The passage states that streaming and ranking reinforce the inequality the Finance Minister warned about in his Budget speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Streaming and ranking serve to reinforce the inequality the Finance Minister warned about in his Budget speech.

sections.label: Reserves, NIRC and GST debate
sections.summary: The passage describes public conversations on social protection and reserves, and proposals to raise the NIRC to 60% to stave off the GST hike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some very important and healthy conversations are taking place within our society about social protection and the size and use of our reserves, estimated in The Straits Times last week to be in excess of a trillion dollars – I will say that again in excess of a trillion dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some arguments have been made in public for the NIRC to be increased to 60% to stave off the GST hike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After such infrastructure has been completed, the NIRC can return to 50% and some portion of the revenue earned from such infrastructure can also be returned to the reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Such proposals leave more scope for the Government to hold back from increasing regressive taxes like the GST, which also hit middle-income Singaporeans with young children and elderly parents the hardest, mainly because offset packages announced by the Government inherently target the low-income and needy more, and correctly so.

sections.label: Carbon tax revenue confirmation
sections.summary: The passage states the Government confirmed the carbon tax would bring an additional $1 billion a year of revenue after implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, the Government was able to confirm that the imposition of the carbon tax would bring an additional $1 billion a year of revenue after implementation.

sections.label: Workers' Party unable to support GST hike
sections.summary: The passage states the Workers' Party cannot support the GST hike announcement now, citing missing details on expenditure, reserves and offset packages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of the absence of such details, the Workers' Party is unable to support the announcement of the GST hike at this moment in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is because of the lack of clarity surrounding projected expenditure when the Government raises GST in future and the relative lack of information on whether there is scope for the reserves to better support Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, as the Prime Minister told the media some years ago when the GST was raised from 3% in response to initial objections from the Workers' Party, we would also need some understanding of the Government's offset package for the low-income and middle-income should the GST be raised ─ information which the Government has not released thus far.

sections.label: Security of elderly Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage states elderly Singaporeans should not feel insecure in old age, especially on healthcare, and should be respected and looked after.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Equally, the security of elderly Singaporeans, each generation a pioneer generation of an improbable country in its own right, should not be made to feel insecure in their old age, particularly when it comes to healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Instead, they should be respected for what they have done for Singapore and looked after in their golden years.

sections.label: Social Development spending share growth
sections.summary: Social Development held the largest spending share, rising to nearly half by 2017, with growth accelerating to 10% a year from 2005 to 2017.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Of the four main areas of spending, Social Development accounted for the largest share of 38%, above the other areas, namely Security and External Relations, Economic Development and Government Administration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By 2017, its share had risen to nearly half of total Government spending, more than twice that of the share of expenditures on Economic Development.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From 1997 to 2005, Social Development expenditures grew at an annual rate of 3.7% per annum, below that of expenditures of Security and External Relations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From 2005 to 2017, however, the rate of growth of Social Development expenditures jumped to 10% a year.

sections.label: United States TARP rescue programme
sections.summary: The United States assigned US$700 billion to the Troubled Asset Relief Program, and all amounts spent on toxic assets were recovered in full.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At a critical point of the crisis, for example, the United States mounted a massively expensive rescue programme for its financial sector by assigning US$700 billion, to what was then known as the Troubled Asset Relief Program or TARP.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As it turned out, all the amounts spent in the purchase of what had been toxic assets were subsequently recovered in full as the assets regained values.

sections.label: 2009 Resilience Package reserve withdrawal
sections.summary: The 2009 Resilience Package included an unprecedented $4.9 billion withdrawal from the reserves, which was returned in full after strong recovery.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The sums assigned to the Resilience Package of 2009 by then-Finance Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam included an unprecedented withdrawal of $4.9 billion from the reserves.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The full amount of that was returned as a result of the strong recovery.

sections.label: Longer-term view and spending plans
sections.summary: He asked Singaporeans to take a longer-term view and said the Government will spend more on healthcare and infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: He asked Singaporeans to take a longer-term view, and set out our strategic challenges clearly and plainly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: He indicated that the Government will spend more on healthcare by building more hospitals, polyclinics, nursing homes and eldercare centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Government will also spend more on infrastructure projects like the rail network, construction of Terminal 5, Tuas Port as well as the High Speed Rail.

sections.label: GST increase timing
sections.summary: The GST increase is planned for 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The GST increase is planned for 2021 to 2025.

sections.label: Advance notice of GST increase
sections.summary: The Government gave three years' advance notice that it would raise revenue by increasing GST by 2% to maintain healthcare, security and social spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Instead, the Government is giving three years' advance notice that in order to maintain the spending on healthcare, security and other social spending, they would need to raise revenue by increasing GST by 2%.

sections.label: GST Voucher scheme commitments
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance committed to enhancing the permanent GST Voucher scheme and to a $2 billion top-up to the GST Voucher Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance has committed to enhancing the permanent GST Voucher scheme and he has also committed to make a $2 billion top-up to the GST Voucher Fund.

sections.label: Budget figures two years
sections.summary: Last year was $14.61 billion and this year the Budget is $15.85 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Last year was $14.61 billion and this year the Budget is $15.85 billion.

sections.label: Committee Against Profiteering and borrowing
sections.summary: It asks whether a Committee Against Profiteering will be set up before the GST increase and why borrowing is necessary given large reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In previous years, when GST was increased, a Committee Against Profiteering (CAP) was set up to combat any illegal profiteering due to a GST increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Would there be a similar committee set up before the GST increase is implemented?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This will help spread the cost of certain large investments over more years." Can the Minister clarify why is it necessary to borrow, considering our large reserves?

sections.label: Lease sale cut-off period
sections.summary: The cut-off period for including a lease as a sale is a 10-year lease, and land sold is not sold in perpetuity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: In fact, the cut-off period when you include a lease as a sale is actually a 10-year lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: In reply to Ms Sylvia Lim, when a land is sold, whether it is on a 99-year lease or otherwise, it is not sold in perpetuity.

sections.label: Proceeds of 99-year land sale
sections.summary: When land is sold for 99 years, the proceeds of sale for that 99 years will be gone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: When you sell a land for 99 years, then the proceeds of sale for that 99 years will be gone.

sections.label: Spending for future generations
sections.summary: This generation is spending money for the future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: Yes, that is why, in this generation, you are spending money for the future generations.

sections.label: Ministry block budget growth rate
sections.summary: From FY2019, Ministries' block budget growth rate is cut from 0.4 to 0.3 times GDP growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From FY2019, the rate of growth for the block budgets of Ministries will be reduced from 0.4 times of GDP growth to 0.3 times.

sections.label: Goods and Services Tax adjustment timing
sections.summary: The Government would not raise GST immediately but at least three years later, giving time to adapt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As for the adjustment of the Goods and Services Tax, this has been widely speculated before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It turned out that the Government would not immediately raise the GST, but would do so at least three years later, giving sufficient time to businesses and consumers to adapt.

sections.label: GST on imported services
sections.summary: In two years, businesses buying imported services from overseas would pay GST; Singapore imported nearly S$225 billion of services in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has also announced that in two years' time, businesses that purchase imported services from overseas would also have to pay GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Department of Statistics, Singapore imported close to S$225 billion worth of services in 2016.

sections.label: Donation deduction extension
sections.summary: A deduction due to cease this year is extended three years; some businesses hope it rises to 300%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This deduction was originally supposed to cease at the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is now going to be extended for another three years to encourage more companies to give back to society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some businesses hope the Government could take a further step to raise the deduction to 300%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This could encourage even more people to make generous donations, contributing both money and effort to build a more caring and united society.

sections.label: Male-female median income gap
sections.summary: The median monthly income gap between men and women stayed around 18% to 19%, women earning about $610 less.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The gap in median monthly income between male and female has remained at around 18% to 19%, with women earning some $610 less than men.

sections.label: CPF LIFE gender payout gap
sections.summary: Men are estimated to get 25% more CPF LIFE income than women; health and social service has a large pay gap.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Using the CPF LIFE Payout Estimator on the CPF Board website, my estimate is that, on the average, men will be getting 25% more income than women from CPF LIFE due to the gender pay gap.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Health and social service is still a sector that has one of the largest gender pay gaps, with women earning around $1,540 a month less than men.

sections.label: Nurses median gross monthly income
sections.summary: Mid-2016 MOM data shows median gross monthly income of all full-time employed residents is $4,056, while nurses earn $4,300.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Based on mid-2016 data from MOM, the median gross monthly income from work of all full-time employed residents is $4,056, while the figure for nurses is $4,300.

sections.label: Recognition and reward for unpaid caregiving
sections.summary: The first issue is recognition and reward for unpaid caregiving, with over 210,000 caregivers estimated in 2004.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The first issue is recognition and reward for unpaid caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was estimated that there were over 210,000 caregivers in 2004.

sections.label: Survey of informal caregiving older adults
sections.summary: A 2013 national survey of informal caregiving for adults aged 75 and above found 55.6% of caregivers worked and averaged 38 care hours weekly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In a national survey of informal caregiving of older adults aged 75 and above presented in 2013, only 55.6% of the caregivers reported that they were working full-time or part-time and the caregivers reported they spent an average of 38 hours a week in providing care.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Among the three problems of lack of family support, negative financial impact and negative impact on schedule and health, caregivers rated financial impact as the heaviest burden, followed closely by negative impact on schedule and health.

sections.label: Caregiver support centres at SCCs
sections.summary: During COS 2017, the member asked for caregiver support centres at Senior Care Centres and noted AIC's three-year pilot and AICareLinks centres.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last year, during COS 2017, I asked the Government to provide better support to caregivers of seniors by setting up caregiver support centres at Senior Care Centres (SCCs).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I was glad to hear from Senior Minister of State Amy Khor that the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) has started a three-year pilot since September 2015 to embed caregiver support services in five SCCs, and that AIC had also started AICareLinks centres at five hospitals and its office at Maxwell Road for caregivers to receive advice on services and schemes.

sections.label: CPF balances of women over 60
sections.summary: In 2016, it was reported that for those over 60, the average CPF balance for women is only 69% that of men.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2016, it was reported that for those over 60 years of age, the average CPF balance for women is only 69% that of men.

sections.label: Relative poverty among working elderly
sections.summary: Another study estimated the relative poverty rate among the working elderly jumped from 13% in 1995 to 41% in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Another study estimated that the relative poverty rate among the working elderly had jumped from 13% in 1995 to 41% in 2011.

sections.label: Tiered payouts and flat size
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether tiered payouts signal families to downsize flats, and says needy seniors should get $750 a quarter regardless of flat size.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Is the tiered payout signalling to the family that they should downsize the flat to better support their seniors?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I believe needy seniors should receive $750 a quarter, regardless of the size of the HDB flat where they live.

sections.label: Gender-differentiated ElderShield premiums
sections.summary: Gender-differentiated ElderShield premiums reflect this, compounding the gender income gap and greater financial insecurity faced by women.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The gender-differentiated ElderShield premiums reflect this but, again, this means it compounds the gender income gap and greater financial insecurity faced by women.

sections.label: Heng Swee Keat on gender budgeting
sections.summary: Minister Heng Swee Keat said the Government accounts for policy impact on segments including gender and targets benefits at those in need.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Heng Swee Keat replied to the question saying that in the design, planning and delivery of programmes, the Government accounts for the impact of policies on different segments of society, including gender, and target benefits at those in need and that Government policies have, over the years, enabled the advancement of women in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I read this reply positively as the Government does do some form of gender budgeting for its programmes, though it is not formalised as such.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As I have made the case in this speech, gender equality is not just an aspiration, but a need.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is a need because, whether absolutely or relatively, the financial security of women through their career from young workers to would-be mothers to caregivers to seniors is paramount to the mitigation of neediness among our ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is a need because gender equality is one of the key upstream solutions to the downstream challenges of ageing and where opportunities for successful ageing of our seniors are shaped and forged.

sections.label: PMETs, ageing population, unemployment
sections.summary: PMET employees are more than half the workforce, the population and local workforce are ageing, and unemployment is 2% to 3%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: PMET employees comprise more than half of our workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We now have a rapidly ageing population and local workforce partly due to the Baby Boom generation effect, while our unemployment rate of 2% to 3% is much lower than that of 1965 in Singapore, or when we compare with most other countries currently, and our industrial relations are stable.

sections.label: Below-15 equals above-65 citizens
sections.summary: For the first time, the proportion of citizens below 15 equalled those above 65, with 2030 estimates of 11% and 27%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: For the first time in our history, the proportion of our citizen population below 15 years old equaled that of our citizen population above 65 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: By one estimate, by the year 2030, the below-15 segment might constitute, say, 11% of the population whereas the above-65 portion could be 27%.

sections.label: Shrinking workforce narrows tax base
sections.summary: Attrition from skills obsolescence and mismatch is excluded, and the shrinking citizen workforce will narrow the personal income tax base, straining Government revenues.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: That does not include attrition from the workforce due to skills obsolescence and mismatch.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This shrinking of the citizen workforce will narrow the personal income tax base, adding strain to Government revenues.

sections.label: Mature workers and retirement age
sections.summary: Longer employment of mature workers helps Government revenues and delays taxpayer support, so Tripartite Partners extended Retirement Age and Re-employment Age to 67 from July 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Conversely, the longer our mature workers can remain employed and earning, the more they can help contribute towards Government revenues and also support their own needs and thus helping to delay and reduce the need for the general taxpayers and younger citizens and companies to have to chip in earlier than necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: It is also for this reason that the Tripartite Partners have agreed over the years to extend, first, the statutory Retirement Age, and then to introduce Re-employment and, most recently, to raise the Re-employment Age ceiling from 65 to 67 effective July 2017.

sections.label: Technology displacing jobs
sections.summary: Some estimates say up to 25% of jobs in the current economy may be altered or displaced by technology in the coming 20 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Some estimates say up to 25% of jobs in the current economy may be altered or displaced by technology in the coming 20 years.

sections.label: Workers learning skills, Industry Transformation Maps
sections.summary: Workers need to learn skills at risk and skills to pick up, making expeditious implementation of Industry Transformation Maps for key industries critical.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In this context, workers need to and want to learn what are the skills at risk and what are the skills they need to pick up, and where they can do so efficiently and cost-effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This is where the expeditious implementation of the industry transformation Maps for key industries will be critical.

sections.label: Tripartite Committee beyond age 67
sections.summary: With the Retirement Age extension to 67 fully implemented, a Tripartite Committee should be convened to consider the road ahead beyond 67.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
