sentences.text: For all the above reasons and given that the recommendation of the Tripartite Committee on the Extension of the Retirement Age to 67 has been fully implemented, there is, therefore, cause, in my view, for another Tripartite Committee to be convened to consider the road ahead, beyond 67.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I, therefore, call for the forming of such a Tripartite Committee and would like to propose that its terms of reference could include the following.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Thirdly, if the statutory age and re-employment age band are still assessed to be necessary, clarify the conditions under which the re-employment ceiling of 67 could be further raised and to what long-term targeted age.

sections.label: SkillsFuture for the Digital Workplace
sections.summary: The newly introduced SkillsFuture for the Digital Workplace is a good example of what needs to be done, and more should be done.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The newly introduced SkillsFuture for the Digital Workplace is a good example of what needs to be done in this regard, and I hope and call for more to be done.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps funding
sections.summary: The Industry Transformation Maps help companies and workers understand and prepare for this future, with $4.5 billion committed for this effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) are important guides to help companies and workers understand and prepare for this future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We have committed $4.5 billion for this effort.

sections.label: SBF survey on ITMs
sections.summary: An SBF survey found companies call ITMs a good initiative but about half are unclear on transformation processes, and one in four are slow to transform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In a survey done by the Singapore Business Federation (SBF), companies said that ITMs are a good initiative but about half of these companies are not so clear on what the transformation processes entail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One in four companies are slow to transform their businesses and some have not digitised any part of their businesses at all.

sections.label: Young NTUC ITM awareness survey
sections.summary: A January 2018 Young NTUC survey of about 400 students found around 83% had not heard about the ITMs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In a recent survey done by Young NTUC in January 2018 on about 400 students in the universities and private educational institutions revealed that around 83% have not heard about the ITMs.

sections.label: Seed funding for SME internships
sections.summary: The Government is called on to help SMEs with seed funding for internship opportunities managed by intermediaries such as NTUC or trade associations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Furthermore, to increase youth involvement in SMEs, we also call on the Government to try to help SMEs by providing seed funding to create internship opportunities, and these opportunities can be managed by intermediaries, such as NTUC or the trade associations.

sections.label: Support for families with dependants
sections.summary: Families face childcare and eldercare costs, so subsidies and support should be reviewed and mandatory eldercare or family care leave considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Such families would have to cope with the stresses and rising costs of looking after children and meet the needs of healthcare and other forms of care for their aged parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Therefore, we need to review how our subsidies and support for childcare and student care are structured, especially for parents with more than one young child and also elderly parents to take care of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As these responsibilities must be juggled and balanced with their careers, could the Government also consider making eldercare or family care leave mandatory in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This could provide some relief to Singaporeans who must take care of family members who are not covered by childcare leave or parental leave.

sections.label: PMET layoffs and re-employment difficulty
sections.summary: Seventy percent of those laid off in 2016 and 2017 were PMETs, and more degrees and older age make finding employment after layoff harder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Seventy percent of those laid off in 2016 and 2017 were PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The trend is that the more degrees you have and the older you are, the more difficult for you to find employment after you have been laid off, are terminated from or leave your employment.

sections.label: Citibank smart banking branch jobs
sections.summary: At the Labour Movement's Future Jobs, Skills and Training Forum, Citibank shared it set up its first smart banking branch four years ago and began eliminating jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: During our Labour Movement’s recent Future Jobs, Skills and Training Forum last month, Citibank shared that four years ago, they set up their first smart banking branch and started eliminating jobs.

sections.label: Skills half-life five years
sections.summary: The half-life of skills is about five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The half-life of skills is about five years.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit and employer training funding
sections.summary: It asks whether employers could get a SkillsFuture credit like the $500 for individuals to send workers for training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The biggest challenges involve the creation of ways to help people learn new skills and then rethinking how the labour market operates to enable employers and employees to move in more agile ways to fill up new positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We have $500 of SkillsFuture credit for individuals to encourage individual-initiated training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Why not take the employer-supported training funding formula, like giving the employers a similar SkillsFuture credit, for them to send their workers for training and skills upgrading?

sections.label: Retraining workers through bank conversion programme
sections.summary: It urges retraining existing workers, citing three local banks training over 1,000 local workers through an in-house professional conversion programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Best of all, re-train, up-skill and multi-skill their existing workers so that they, too, can take on these new roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We have started this in the financial sector, with the three local banks embarking on training more than 1,000 of their local workers through the in-house professional conversion programme (PCP) as part of the industry transformation and Tripartite efforts of the financial sector.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps are blueprints
sections.summary: The 23 Industry Transformation Maps are developed by the sector but are merely blueprints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The 23 Industry Transformation Maps are developed by the sector, but they are merely blueprints.

sections.label: Information asymmetry impedes future-skilling
sections.summary: Engagements with stakeholders found information asymmetry was an underlying factor impeding future-skilling and job mismatches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In engagements with various stakeholders, we found that one of the underlying factors impeding future-skilling and job mismatches was information asymmetry.

sections.label: Union bargaining for healthcare workers
sections.summary: The Union has collectively bargained for nursing and non-nursing healthcare workers, negotiating salary scale increases, annual increments and bonuses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: For the past decade, the Union has been collectively bargaining on behalf of all healthcare workers whether they are workers in the nursing as well in the non-nursing areas in our various healthcare clusters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We have reviewed salary scales on several occasions and had many heated negotiations and collective bargaining with our employers and have done a lot of work to raise wages as well as salaries and improving career conditions and career progression for healthcare workers, both nursing and non-nursing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Their collective agreements are publicly available documents which Members can refer to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We have since negotiated increases in salary scales and made good progress in terms of annual increments and bonuses.

sections.label: Tripartite partners and wages
sections.summary: Speaker urges Tripartite Partners to work on all fronts so pay and interests are fair, responsible and progressive, and voices concern over Daniel Goh's suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: But I think it is important to work together as Tripartite Partners and also on all fronts to make sure that, not just pay and wages but also their interests, are not just fair and responsible but also progressive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I also want to express a bit of my concern over Assoc Prof Daniel Goh's various suggestions to raise wages, Silver support, healthcare spending.

sections.label: Healthcare ITM launch
sections.summary: On 8 November 2017, Minister Gan Kim Yong launched the Healthcare ITM, which mapped strategies to steer the healthcare industry and workforce towards better skills and work.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 8 November 2017, Minister Gan Kim Yong, launched the Healthcare ITM which mapped out the key strategies to steer the healthcare industry and workforce towards better skills and better work, so that they can deliver better care for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Skills frameworks for healthcare professions
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Singapore has begun developing skills frameworks for six healthcare professions: Physiotherapy, Speech Therapy, Occupational Therapy, Nursing, Patient Service Associate and Pharmacy Technician.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture Singapore has started its work on the development of the skills framework for six healthcare professions, namely, Physiotherapy, Speech Therapy, Occupational Therapy, Nursing, Patient Service Associate and Pharmacy Technician.

sections.label: Progressive wage model in healthcare
sections.summary: One way would be to embark on the progressive wage model across all levels of healthcare professions.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One way would be to embark on the progressive wage model (PWM) across all levels of healthcare professions.

sections.label: Attracting locals, non-practising nurses study
sections.summary: Change is critical to attract more locals into healthcare, and a study on nearly 4,000 non-practising nurses would be worthwhile.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is critical for us to change so as to attract more locals into the healthcare profession.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It would also be worthwhile to conduct a study on the nearly 4,000 non-practising nurses to understand their reasons for exiting from this profession and what would make them return as a practising nurse.

sections.label: Healthcare Academy objectives
sections.summary: The Healthcare Academy has two key objectives: enhanced skills training for healthcare professionals in the Healthcare ITM, and standardised foundational core skills training, especially in the ILTC sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The two key objectives of the Healthcare Academy are: one, to provide enhanced skills training to all healthcare professionals identified in the Healthcare ITM; and two, to standardise the foundational core skills training for identified healthcare professionals, especially in the ILTC sector.

sections.label: Study on working women's plight
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to commission a study on the plight of working women to understand issues across industries.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On mandating the right to request for flexible work arrangements, I urge the Government to commission a study on the plight of these working women so as to better understand the issues faced by different industries.

sections.label: Mandating right to request FWA
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a change agent among companies and for the Government to consider mandating the right to request flexible work arrangements if persuasion fails.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must have a change agent, early adopter, amongst companies and industries that have successfully rolled out FWA to share with the rest of the sectors and be a catalyst for change.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also call upon the Government to consider mandating the right to request for flexible work arrangements if all efforts – I repeat – if all efforts to persuade employers in this aspect fail.

sections.label: Young mother given ultimatum
sections.summary: A supervisor gave a young mother an ultimatum to resign if she failed to make other childcare arrangements, due to KPIs such as waiting time.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Having been bogged down with KPIs, such as waiting time, the supervisor gave the young mother an ultimatum to resign from the job if she failed to make other childcare arrangements.

sections.label: Gestational diabetes and breastfeeding
sections.summary: Singapore has among the highest gestational diabetes rates globally, and longer breastfeeding correlated with reduced risk of Type-2 diabetes in women.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore has among the highest gestational diabetes rates globally.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Women with gestational diabetes are up to seven times more likely to develop Type-2 diabetes.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, longer durations of breastfeeding showed a correlation with reduction in the risk of women developing Type-2 diabetes.

sections.label: WorkPro grant for lactation facilities
sections.summary: The WorkPro Work-Life Grant Developmental Grant lets owners of post-1990 buildings tap funding capped at S$20,000 for publicly accessible lactation facilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, the WorkPro Work-Life Grant – Developmental Grant allows owners of post-1990 buildings to tap on the funding, capped at S$20,000, to put in publicly accessible lactation facilities.

sections.label: Types of self-employed persons
sections.summary: This new form of employment should not be confused with wrongly classified workers, and there are generally three types of self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This new form of employment should not be confused with workers who have been wrongly classified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There are generally three types of self-employed persons: first group are those who chose this profession as the preferred choice; second group are those who chose it not as a preferred choice; and third, there may be those who may have been wrongly classified as freelancers.

sections.label: Freelancers and platform intermediaries
sections.summary: Freelancers can pitch to more clients through intermediaries, which are not obliged to act as employers by making CPF contributions or providing insurance or medical leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Freelancers, on the other hand, get to pitch and market their services to a bigger pool of prospective clients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These intermediaries, however, are not obliged to perform the roles of an employer, such as making CPF contributions, or providing workplace insurance cover or medical leave for the freelancers.

sections.label: Reviewing platform intermediary operations
sections.summary: After a light regulatory approach, it may be timely for Government agencies to review platform intermediaries' operations and consider giving them more responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Having previously taken a light regulatory approach, perhaps it is more timely now for the Government agencies to review the operations of such platform intermediaries and consider getting them to take on more responsibilities.

sections.label: Tripartite workgroup for workers
sections.summary: Following a survey, the Minister last year announced a Tripartite workgroup formed in March 2017 to study issues faced by this group of workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Following that survey, the Minister last year announced a Tripartite workgroup that was formed in March 2017 to study the issues faced by this group of workers.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model sectors
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model has improved wages and skills of thousands of low-wage workers in the cleaning, security and landscape sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Model (PWM) is one initiative that has improved the wages and skills of thousands of low-wage workers in the cleaning, security and landscape sectors.

sections.label: Built-in wage increase recommendations
sections.summary: Tripartite Committees recently recommended a built-in wage increase for cleaning and security workers so real wages are not eroded by inflation or down-waging on contract renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Recently, the Tripartite Committees have made recommendations to have a built-in wage increase for workers in the cleaning and security sectors to ensure their real wages are not eroded by inflation or experience "down-waging" when their contracts are renewed.

sections.label: Reviewing CPF for older workers
sections.summary: Union leaders felt strongly it is about time for Tripartite Partners to set up a committee to review the employer's CPF contribution for older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: First, the union leaders felt strongly that it is about time for our Tripartite Partners to set up a committee to review the employer's CPF contribution for older workers.

sections.label: Universal employer CPF contribution rate
sections.summary: It suggests exploring one universal rate for employer's CPF contribution until age 65, noting many still service mortgages and care for aged parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: There are also many who still need to service their mortgage loans, as well as take care of their aged parents who are living longer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, it may not be a bad idea to explore the possibility of working towards having one universal rate for employer's CPF contribution till the age of 65 years old.

sections.label: Mandatory Annual Wage Supplement
sections.summary: It states that mandating AWS could raise low-wage workers' salaries by 8.3% and help reduce Singapore's widening income gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Mandating AWS could bring about an increase of 8.3% to the salaries of low-wage workers ‒ and help reduce the widening income gap present in Singapore.

sections.label: Employment Act medical coverage
sections.summary: It states the Employment Act only requires employers to pay consultation fees, and union leaders want full non-chronic outpatient treatment costs covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The current provision of the Employment Act only requires employers to pay for the medical consultation fees when a worker sees a doctor for outpatient treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, the union leaders felt that the Tripartite Partners should consider amending the Employment Act to include better medical coverage for workers, by making employers pay for the full cost of non-chronic outpatient treatment at polyclinics or company-appointed clinics.

sections.label: CPF review and mandatory AWS
sections.summary: It calls on Tripartite Partners to review CPF for one universal employer rate up to age 65 and to make the 13th month bonus mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In order to ensure that low-wage workers have enough savings for their retirement, I would like to call on the Tripartite Partners to form a review committee on CPF to explore the possibility of having one universal rate for employer’s CPF contribution for all workers up to the age of 65 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I would also like to suggest making the 13th month bonus or the Annual Wage Supplement mandatory, in order to boost the retirement savings of low-wage workers.

sections.label: Total fertility rate 2016
sections.summary: It states Singapore's total fertility rate dipped to 1.2 in 2016 despite more marriages and Government parenthood incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our total fertility rate dipped to just 1.2 in 2016, despite having a relatively higher number of marriages and a slew of Government incentives to encourage parenthood.

sections.label: Workplace fatalities dropped 2017
sections.summary: It states MOM reported workplace fatalities fell to 42 in 2017, the lowest in over a decade, lowering the fatality rate to 1.2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Earlier this month, the MOM reported that the number of workplace fatalities in 2017 had dropped to 42.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is the lowest figure in over a decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This lowers our workplace fatality rate from 1.9 per 100,000 workers in 2014 to 1.2 in 2017.

sections.label: Workplace injuries and fatalities
sections.summary: MOM's report showed workplace fatalities fell in 2017 but workplace injury cases remained high, with close to 12,500 cases and 574 serious injuries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While workplace fatalities have decreased in 2017, MOM’s report also showed that the number of workplace injury cases remains high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There were close to 12,500 workplace injury cases in 2017, with 574 workers sustaining serious injuries.

sections.label: NTWU brown rice canteens
sections.summary: The National Transport Workers' Union, which operates 45 canteens islandwide, introduced brown rice at a subsidised rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To address that, the National Transport Workers' Union (NTWU), which operates 45 canteens islandwide, introduced brown rice at a subsidised rate.

sections.label: Bus captain health screening
sections.summary: A joint project with HPB and public transport operators screened 1,000 bus captains; 80% failed at least one indicator, and a third passed all three after six months of coaching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In a joint project with the HPB and our public transport operators, the union organised a free health screening for 1,000 of our bus captains, testing them for their blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Sadly, but not unexpected, 80% of the bus captains tested failed at least one of the three health indicators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What is heartening to note is that after going through a period of health coaching, a third of these bus captains managed to achieve a pass in all three health indicators after six months.

sections.label: Stamp duty tax revenues
sections.summary: The stamp duty is a progressive, simple tax that lets the Government reap about $400 million in tax revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The stamp duty is a progressive, simple tax which allows the Government to reap about $400 million in tax revenues is just one such example.

sections.label: Simple socialism and social needs
sections.summary: Simple socialism requires addressing real social needs, not just felt deprivation relative to others; he is 52 and earns less than $2,700 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Our simple socialism, however, requires us to address not just felt deprivation relative to others, but real social needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: He is 52 years old and earns less than $2,700 a month.

sections.label: Housing loan refinancing difficulty
sections.summary: The rate is very high because current housing loan interest is around 2%, and no banks would refinance his 2-room flat loan of less than $100,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is very high, because the current housing loan interest is around 2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: He went to all the major banks to try and refinance but there were no takers because his is a 2-room flat and the amount is less than $100,000.

sections.label: HDB loan refinancing rules
sections.summary: Peter has never taken an HDB loan, and rules bar those with bank housing loans from refinancing with an HDB loan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Peter has never taken a loan from HDB but our current rules are such that if you have taken a housing loan from a bank, you will not be allowed to refinance your flat with a housing loan from HDB.

sections.label: Means-tested shift to HDB loans
sections.summary: The passage proposes allowing a means-tested way to shift private loans back to HDB, especially given high interest rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: There is an easy way to break this false choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We could, for example, allow a means-tested way to facilitate the shift of private loans back to HDB, especially when their interest rates are so high above HDB rates.

sections.label: Peter's benefits and means test
sections.summary: Peter is grateful for Government help, but now pays $166.50 monthly, lost other benefits, and his means test is $675 per capita.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: He is very appreciative and grateful for all these help from the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This year, however, he has to pay $166.50 a month, and he has lost all the other benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The means test is at $675 per capita a month ─ Peter came in at $750 a month.

sections.label: Interest and overtime benefit losses
sections.summary: Peter pays more interest than his rich neighbour and loses benefits by a whisker of overtime pay, which can be changed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: He pays more in interest than his rich neighbour – we can change this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: He loses benefits by a whisker of overtime pay – we can change this, too.

sections.label: Disruptive industries reshaping economy
sections.summary: Disruptive industries using new technology or business models, like the sharing economy, may destroy old jobs and companies while creating new ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The world is seeing the emergence of disruptive industries using new technology or new business models, like the sharing economy, industries that may reshape the economy – destroying old jobs and stodgy companies, but also creating new ones.

sections.label: Emerging disruptive technologies list
sections.summary: The passage lists emerging technologies and business models disrupting the world, including big data analytics, IoT, AI, drones, robotics, 3D printing and others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Some emerging technologies and business models that are disrupting the world include big data analytics, the Internet of Things (iOT) which collects big data, artificial intelligence (AI) which is fed by big data, drones, autonomous vehicles, robotics including social robotics, 3D printing, virtual and augmented reality, cloud computing, crypto-currencies, genetic editing and renewable energy technologies like cutting-edge solar cells coupled with cutting-edge battery technology.

sections.label: ASEAN population share
sections.summary: ASEAN has over 600 million people, about 8% of the world's population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: ASEAN has over 600 million people, about 8% of the world’s population.

sections.label: Grab cities in Indonesia
sections.summary: Grab operates in over 50 cities across Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Today, Grab operates in over 50 cities across Indonesia.

sections.label: Singapore regional component supply
sections.summary: Singapore could produce and supply the region advanced, high value-added and IP-sensitive components, materials and services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore could also produce and supply to the region the most advanced, high value-added and IP-sensitive components, materials and services.

sections.label: ASEAN innovation test-bed project
sections.summary: Singapore could suggest a bold, visionary project to transform the ASEAN region into a test-bed for innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My fourth point is that Singapore could consider suggesting a bold, visionary project that aims to transform the ASEAN region itself into a test-bed for innovation.

sections.label: Testing autonomous vehicles
sections.summary: Singapore could help test-bed autonomous vehicles, pioneering refuelling stations and the associated regulatory framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore could help to test-bed autonomous vehicles, pioneering the establishment and maintenance of refuelling stations as well as the associated regulatory framework.

sections.label: Government gig economy policy
sections.summary: A question asks how the Government views the gig economy and the broad thrust of its policy towards the sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Could he touch on how the Government views the gig economy and what would be the broad thrust of Government policy towards this sector? 3.17 pm

sections.label: HSBC Belt and Road projection
sections.summary: HSBC projected the Belt and Road Initiative will change global trade with 900 projects and trillions in investments, infrastructure and trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: HSBC projected that China's Belt and Road Initiative will further change the face of global trade, with 900 planned projects, $4 trillion of investments, $8 trillion of infrastructure and $2.5 trillion of trade annually.

sections.label: Singaporeans speaking Mandarin at home
sections.summary: A 2016 Government survey found less than 35% of Singaporeans spoke Mandarin at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: In a 2016 Government survey, it was found that less than 35% of Singaporeans spoke Mandarin at home.

sections.label: Refusal to hire Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker says they are used to comfort and cannot take hardships, and now does not want to hire Singaporeans at all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: They are used to comfort and cannot take hardships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Now I don't want to hire Singaporeans at all.

sections.label: Lee Kuan Yew on bilingualism
sections.summary: Lee Kuan Yew wrote in his book that Singaporeans are more bilingual but too few understand Chinese deeply enough to deal effectively with them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, the late Minister Mentor Lee Kuan Yew made this comment in his book "My Lifelong Challenge" more than 10 years ago: "While Singaporeans are more bilingual than before, we do not have enough who understand the Chinese at a deep enough level to deal effectively with them.

sections.label: Levelling up second language proficiency
sections.summary: The next phase of development requires levelling up second language proficiency beyond a textbook subject to a live tool in commerce and business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Our next phase of development will require us to level up our second language proficiency beyond a textbook subject to a live tool used in commerce and business.

sections.label: Bilingualism as competitiveness component
sections.summary: Being bilingual or trilingual has to be a key component of overall competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Being bilingual or trilingual has to be a key component of our overall competitiveness.

sections.label: Developing talent for China
sections.summary: The speaker calls for developing talent in public and private sectors who understand Chinese ways, suggesting the three G-to-G projects as internship platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Going forward, we need to systematically develop our pool of talents, both in public and private sectors, who would study and understand Chinese ways of doing things.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: I would go further to suggest that our three G-to-G projects – Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park (SIP), Tianjin Eco-City and Chongqing Connectivity Initiative – offer ready platforms for our Public Service Leadership Officers for a meaningful period of internship and exchange.

sections.label: Multilingualism and regional connections
sections.summary: The passage states that being multilingual and deeply connected to the regional hinterlands must be a strategic priority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Being multilingual and deeply connected to the regional hinterlands must be our strategic priority.

sections.label: Social contract with people
sections.summary: The passage quotes the Minister saying it is a means to build a better home and quality of life, forming a social contract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The answer comes in the Minister's next line, which I quote: “It is a means to build a better home and provide a better quality of life for all our people.” So, there is a certain social contract, forged between the people of Singapore and the Government.

sections.label: Collective responsibility quote
sections.summary: The passage quotes DPM Tharman Shanmugaratnam's 2015 Budget Speech on complementing personal effort with stronger collective responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If I may quote Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam's Budget Speech back in 2015, we seek to "complement a culture of personal effort and responsibility with stronger collective responsibility".

sections.label: Families' financial aid worries
sections.summary: The passage states these families bear a heavy burden and worry that salary increments may disqualify them from financial aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, these families bear a heavy burden on their shoulders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They worry that when they get salary increments they may no longer qualify for financial aid and other assistance.

sections.label: Many helping hands approach
sections.summary: The passage states the Government currently adopts the many helping hands approach to plug gaps where Government schemes deliver less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, the Government has adopted the "many helping hands" approach to plug the gaps where Government schemes are less able to deliver.

sections.label: Meritocracy and eradicating inequality
sections.summary: The passage says meritocracy should be upheld for growth while systematic approaches eradicate inequality so meritocracy is more equitable and all people have a better quality of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While we want to uphold meritocracy to promote growth, we should also then look at systematic approaches to eradicate inequality, so that meritocracy can be more equitable, so that we can help achieve a better quality of life for all people.

sections.label: Reserves belong to Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage states that the accumulated reserves belong to Singaporeans, especially as contributions from older generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The reserves we have accumulated belong to Singaporeans, especially when they are contributions from the older generations.

sections.label: Ong Ye Kung on obstacles
sections.summary: The passage quotes Minister Ong Ye Kung saying the main obstacle is ourselves, our organisations, entrenched processes, bureaucracy and fear of failure, and agrees our biggest stumbling blocks are ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to cite what Minister Ong Ye Kung shared in his keynote speech at the last Public Service Conference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I quote, "The main obstacle is ourselves – our organisation and all our entrenched processes, bureaucracy and a culture of being afraid to fail because all these years we have succeeded." Indeed, our biggest stumbling blocks are ourselves.

sections.label: Safeguarding spaces for discourse
sections.summary: The passage says a functioning democratic system needs safeguarded spaces for discourse to respect differences, be politically expedient, learn from differing views and become stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a functioning democratic system, we need to safeguard spaces for such discourses, not only because we should respect differences, not only because it is politically expedient to do so, but because we can learn from differing views, widen our perspective and become stronger in the process.

sections.label: Democracy beyond votes
sections.summary: The passage states democracy is not just votes and electorates but a system letting different groups pose questions and opinions, start discourse, raise awareness of social problems and make a difference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Democracy is not just about votes and electorates, but a system that allows different groups of people to pose their questions and opinions, to start a discourse, hoping more people will be more aware of our social problems, get involved and make a difference.

sections.label: Patriotism beyond flag-waving
sections.summary: The passage states patriotism is not just flag-waving and National Day celebrations, nor the pursuit to be best, richest, fastest, smartest or most advanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Patriotism is not just about flag-waving and National Day celebrations; patriotism is not about the pursuit to be the best, the richest, the fastest, the smartest or the most advanced.

sections.label: Listening to activists and underserved
sections.summary: It urges allowing values to be challenged and investing in activists' emotional truths before judging and proposing humane, just, equal policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Allow your values to be challenged, be confronted and to invest into the emotional truths of the activists and the underserved, before making judgement and proposing solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Only with vulnerable listening, then the policies formulated can be more humane, more just, more equal.

sections.label: Government AI technology hub investment
sections.summary: It proposes Government investment in an AI technology hub, citing strategic value in public-sector ownership of AI research.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: AI can empower many sectors: drug discovery, factory design, service innovation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I propose that the Government invest in an AI technology hub, in the same way that we invested many years ago in building the Biopolis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Because there is strategic value in Singapore maintaining public-sector ownership in AI research, whether it is intellectual property or the insights.

sections.label: Funding quantum-secured communications research
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government will continue funding research such as the NRF's work at the Centre for Quantum Technologies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: On the flip side, quantum-secured communications are also on the rise – sharing information such that eavesdropping can be detected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, can the Government tell us if we will continue funding research like what the NRF is doing at the Centre for Quantum Technologies?

sections.label: ASEAN common standards as trusted party
sections.summary: It states that as a trusted, neutral first mover Singapore can establish common ASEAN standards in e-payments and data protection.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Furthermore, by being a trusted, neutral party, a trusted first mover, we can establish common standards in ASEAN with our ASEAN partners, whether it is e-payments, data protection across jurisdictions and so on.

sections.label: Digital infrastructure investment and legislation
sections.summary: It says Singapore should prepare early, increase digital infrastructure investment and legislate in advance to become a world-class digital centre.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We should respond appropriately to the situation and prepare early so that we can become a world-class digital centre.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We should increase investment in digital infrastructure and legislate in advance so that Singapore can sustain its reputation of being a safe and reliable hub, hence, becoming the top choice in the region for data storage.

sections.label: Fast-track pathway for unicorn IPOs
sections.summary: It proposes an expedited fast-track pathway for potential unicorns to negotiate an IPO in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As a first step, I propose that we establish an expedited fast-track pathway, so that potential unicorns can quickly negotiate an initial public offering (IPO) in Singapore, especially if the IPO brings strategic value with the company, whether it is the valuation, stimulating the local ecosystem, or growing our national prestige, reputation and position.

sections.label: Industrial-commercial land use and leasing
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to diversify its approach to industrial-commercial land use and leasing, while pricing land appropriately.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Land has to be priced appropriately, but we can be innovative as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I call upon the Government to diversify the approach to industrial-commercial land use and leasing.

sections.label: Nurturing entrepreneurship in schools
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to study how schools can nurture entrepreneurship and skills and facilitate sharing of skills and experiences.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Our school system can help bridge that gap.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, I call upon the Government to study how we can nurture entrepreneurship and skills in our schools, how our education system can facilitate the sharing of skills, the sharing of experiences, so that young Singaporeans have a less steep learning curve on that journey to entrepreneurship because such skills should not just be the domain of those with prior experience or pre-existing social networks.

sections.label: GST increase and tax transfers
sections.summary: The speaker says the GST adjustment is necessary but the Government must keep policy so lower- and middle-income groups receive a positive net transfer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The adjustments in GST is important and necessary to help Singapore secure a robust tax revenue to support our future social spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I believe that while the lower-income and middle-income group will pay more of this consumption tax when GST is eventually increased, the Government must continue its current policy, such that they receive a corresponding increase in tax transfers and subsidies, so that the increase in GST will result in a positive net transfer to this group.

sections.label: Supporting SMEs in upgrading
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the programme supporting SMEs in upgrading and transformation can be ramped up beyond the 650 companies already benefiting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is especially important for our SMEs that might not have the same corporate resources and knowledge as MNCs to initiate large-scale upgrading and transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that the scale of this programme can be ramped up to go beyond supporting the 650 companies that it is already benefiting.

sections.label: ITMs and obsolete jobs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government can use ITMs to identify jobs becoming obsolete and help employees transit into growing sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can the Government use the ITMs to identify jobs that will be made obsolete and redundant in these industries and help employees in those jobs transit into new roles in other sectors where demand for manpower is growing?

sections.label: PHG subsidy for singles
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the PHG for singles buying resale flats near parents be based on a percentage of selling price instead of a fixed amount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the new initiatives in the PHG is the introduction of the $10,000 subsidy for singles who are buying resale flats to live near their parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While this will no doubt encourage singles to live in proximity to their parents, the impact of the subsidy on actual purchases will be different, depending on the differing prices of the estate where the parents live.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, someone whose parents live in a mature estate could expect to pay a lot more for a basic flat to live near their parents, as compared to someone who is buying an equivalent flat to live near their parents in a non-mature estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Instead of a fixed amount, could the Government consider having a PHG that is based on the percentage of the selling price of the resale flat, subject to a minimum of the original base of $10,000 and a maximum ceiling?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This would be helpful for those who have little choice but to buy flats in more mature estates because their parents happen to be living in those estates.

sections.label: Reserve income caution
sections.summary: The speaker says we must be wary about dipping more into our reserve income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, we must be wary about dipping more into our reserve income.

sections.label: Helping seniors monetise assets
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government must actively help seniors monetise their assets to pay for retirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second point is that our Government must actively help our seniors to monetise their assets to pay for their retirement.

sections.label: ITMs long-term transformation plan
sections.summary: The speaker hopes ITMs are recognised as a long-term economic transformation plan and not pushed for immediate results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, I hope we can all recognise that ITMs are a long-term economic transformation plan and not push for immediate results, especially in terms of economic output numbers.

sections.label: ASEAN Secretariat funding suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker suggests Singapore, as ASEAN Chair this year, encourage other major ASEAN economies to increase funding for the ASEAN Secretariat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Beyond the announced measures, I would like to further suggest, as ASEAN Chair this year, that Singapore encourage other major ASEAN economies to increase funding for the ASEAN Secretariat.

sections.label: Shifting tertiary programmes to developing countries
sections.summary: The speaker suggests shifting the balance of tertiary education internships, study trips and exchange programmes towards developing countries, especially ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, we could shift the balance of tertiary education internships, study trips and exchange programmes towards developing countries, especially ASEAN.

sections.label: Student and official interactions
sections.summary: The speaker says we should encourage more interactions between our students and officials from ASEAN countries studying in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Three, we should encourage more interactions between our students and officials from ASEAN countries who are currently studying in Singapore.

sections.label: Teaching ASEAN-specific knowledge
sections.summary: The passage states that teaching of ASEAN-specific knowledge should be encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Four, we should encourage the teaching of ASEAN-specific knowledge.

sections.label: Annual Business ASEAN conference
sections.summary: The passage recommends creating an annual Business ASEAN conference, like the Business China Conference series, to spotlight ASEAN developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My last recommendation is to create an annual Business ASEAN conference, much like the successful Business China Conference series, which put an annual spotlight on the exciting developments in ASEAN.

sections.label: GST raise announced
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance announced that GST will have to be raised in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   The Minister for Finance has announced that the GST will have to be raised in the next few years.

sections.label: Postponing GST increase
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government is considering postponing the GST increase beyond the projected timeframe if future economic performance is better than expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is the Government considering the possibility of postponing the GST increase beyond the projected timeframe if our future economic performance is better than expected?

sections.label: Labour productivity growth
sections.summary: The passage notes that labour productivity grew 4.5% last year, a seven-year high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: (In English): I am heartened to note that our labour productivity grew 4.5% last year, a seven-year high.

sections.label: Wage increases and productivity
sections.summary: The passage asks if the Ministry has details on how much of past wage increases came from the 4.5% productivity increase, and supports extending the Wage Credit Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have details of how much of the wage increases in the past year can be attributed to the 4.5% increase in productivity?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I fully support the decision to extend the Wage Credit Scheme which co-funds salary increases for Singaporean employees, up to a gross monthly wage of $4,000.

sections.label: Ministry budgets and cost-effectiveness
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Ministries can stay within allocated budgets through work design and technology, and suggests annual review of investments instead of pegging budgets to GDP growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is it not possible for each Ministry to continue its operations within the allocated Budget to strive for cost-effectiveness through work design improvements and taking advantage of technological innovations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Instead of pegging departments' budgets to GDP growth, it may be better to review and justify investments and expenditures annually, even in years when there is GDP growth.

sections.label: Infrastructure collaborations and local firms
sections.summary: The passage says infrastructure collaborations are good news if local consultants and construction firms are involved, and notes an Infrastructure Office will bring together local and international firms.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Collaborations on infrastructure development is good news for our construction industry, that is, if there are plans to have local engineering and other consultants as well as construction firms to be actively involved.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that an Infrastructure Office will be established to bring together local and international firms from across the value chain.

sections.label: Full-time secretariat for industry ITMs
sections.summary: The passage argues plans alone are unrealistic and proposes a full-time secretariat for each industry's ITM to visit trade associations, resolve differences and administrative issues, and ensure effective partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is unrealistic to put together a plan on paper and expect everybody to go through with it and resolve the problems by themselves.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Thus, I propose there should be a full-time secretariat for each industry's ITM, to visit the trade associations and speak with the ground, to help resolve differences and administrative issues and ensure that each partnership is as effective and efficient as possible.

sections.label: Home Improvement Programme for HDB flats
sections.summary: The passage describes housing as an integral life asset and expresses disappointment that there is no new commitment to a Home Improvement Programme for HDB flats built after 1986.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First of all, housing, an integral part of our lives and an asset that supposedly gives us financial security in old age.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am disappointed that there is no new commitment to a Home Improvement Programme for HDB flats built after 1986.

sections.label: Buyer's Stamp Duty increase derivation
sections.summary: The passage asks how the decision to raise the Buyer's Stamp Duty for residential properties above $1 million was derived.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to ask how the decision to raise the Buyer's Stamp Duty for residential properties above $1 million was derived.

sections.label: GST increase and profiteering concern
sections.summary: The passage notes the Government announced the GST increase will be implemented between 2021 and 2025 and expresses concern that businesses may raise prices in advance and profiteer.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   The Government has just recently announced that the GST increase will be implemented between 2021 and 2025, but I am concerned that businesses will take the opportunity to increase prices in advance and engage in profiteering.

sections.label: Household income as benchmark
sections.summary: The speaker says household income should not be the sole benchmark, as fixation on it made some applicants ineligible.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Please do not use household income solely as the benchmark, because our fixation on the household income resulted in some applicants becoming ineligible.

sections.label: Silver Housing Bonus and HIP limits
sections.summary: The Silver Housing Bonus requires most proceeds be topped up into CPF, and HIP applies only to units built before 1986.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Even though we have the Silver Housing Bonus, the scheme requires that most of the proceeds be topped up into the CPF and may not meet the needs of all the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As HIP is only applicable to units built before 1986, units built after 1987, although very old, they have not been renovated with low costs.

sections.label: Gig work and drivers
sections.summary: Part-time or freelance gigs will become permanent for some, and Singapore has around 75,000 taxi and private hire drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For others, a series of part-time or freelance gigs will become their permanent reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We have around 75,000 taxi and private hire drivers in Singapore.

sections.label: Gig economy out of necessity
sections.summary: A 2016 McKinsey study found 30% of gig economy workers were there out of necessity and were not happy about it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: According to a 2016 study by McKinsey, 30% of gig economy workers were in the gig economy out of necessity; they had no choice and they were not happy about it.

sections.label: Older and less-educated workers
sections.summary: Of Singapore's 2.2 million labour force, around 700,000 workers are over 50 or have less than Secondary school education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Out of our 2.2 million labour force, around 700,000 workers are over 50 years old or have less than Secondary school education.

sections.label: Alternative revenue sources question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether alternative revenue sources, such as a wealth tax, need to be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Do we need to consider alternative revenue sources, such as a wealth tax?

sections.label: Displaced workers and national response
sections.summary: The speaker says displaced humans need meaningful roles to retain dignity and calls for a serious national conversation from strength.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: There will be many cases where humans will struggle to compete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We need to ensure that the displaced have meaningful roles that will allow them to retain their dignity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I feel truly that we need to tackle this problem head on and decide as a nation on how to respond.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I do not have the answers, but we need to have a serious conversation and not just repeat comforting platitudes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is imperative that we do this from a position of strength.

sections.label: Budget for next 10 years
sections.summary: The speaker says the Budget is not just for the year ahead but deals with the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The most important is that this is a Budget not just for the year ahead but one which deals with the next 10 years.

sections.label: Three megatrends and demographic challenge
sections.summary: The Minister identified three megatrends shaping the future, and the speaker calls the demographic challenge the biggest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Minister rightfully identified the three megatrends that will shape the future, including the move towards Asia, automation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think herein lies opportunities but the biggest challenge is the third – our demographic challenge.

sections.label: Risk of Singapore being irrelevant
sections.summary: The speaker says that if they fail, there is a chance Singapore could be irrelevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we fail, there is a chance that Singapore could be irrelevant.

sections.label: Globalised economy and rice bowl
sections.summary: The speaker says in the globalised economy your rice bowl can be stolen no matter how hard you work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The reality about the globalised economy is that no matter how hard you work, your rice bowl can be stolen at any time.

sections.label: Anticipated tax rises
sections.summary: The speaker notes an anticipated 2% GST rise plus taxes on cigarettes, carbon and other areas, sustainable to at least 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Many of us were anticipating a rise in taxes and it is good to know upfront that the anticipated rise is 2% in GST plus a few other taxes on cigarettes, carbon and other areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is good for us to understand that this is going to be the cost to be sustainable for, say, the next 10 years, at least up to 2025.

sections.label: Selling land capital upfront
sections.summary: The speaker says he once considered the suggestion but agrees it is wrong in principle to sell land and spend that capital upfront.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I should add, I would not laugh this suggestion off because, previously, I had considered this myself at one point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But I agree fundamentally that it is wrong in principle to sell land and spend that capital upfront.

sections.label: Expenses from annual revenues
sections.summary: All expenses should be paid for with annual operating revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: All our expenses should be paid for with our annual operating revenues.

sections.label: Budget and demographic challenges
sections.summary: The Budget shows the Government's plan for ageing population healthcare and infrastructure needs, including tax rises such as GST, and the speaker filed 18 cuts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As our population ages, we will have a much higher demand for healthcare needs at a time when our working population will fall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There will also be a much greater need for infrastructure spending, both to renew ageing infrastructure as well as to build new ones, so Singapore can continue to stay ahead of the curve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, this Budget gives us hope for optimism because it shows the Government’s plan for dealing with these demographic changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This includes rises in taxes, including GST, and looking for other new forms of income to pay for infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Budget sets out a roadmap for dealing with our long-term challenges in the decade ahead and to help Singapore not only overcome these challenges, but to remain a special place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This year, I have 18 specific recommendations for the Government and have filed 18 cuts.

sections.label: Speaking up in Public Service
sections.summary: The speaker is asked whether people get into trouble for speaking up, and those met generally agree they will.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Almost without fail, I will be asked two questions: the first is, "Will I get into trouble if I speak up and share my thoughts with you?" And for those we met, there is a general consensus that people will get into trouble if they speak up in the Public Service.

sections.label: Revamping Public Service appraisal system
sections.summary: A public servant suggestion is to revamp the appraisal system, and the speaker suggests studying the 360-degree appraisal review used by private sector MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One suggestion from the public servants is a revamp of the appraisal system, which, they feel, prevents them from speaking up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I suggest that we redesign the Public Service appraisal system by studying the 360-degree appraisal review used by the private sector in MNCs like Google and Alibaba.

sections.label: Appraisal system and speaking up
sections.summary: Public servants do not speak up, and the speaker says the current appraisal system does not incentivise risk-taking and innovation and suggests changing it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, they do not speak up although their suggestions may, in fact, improve the lives of their fellow countrymen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This current appraisal system does not incentivise risk-taking and innovation, and I suggest we change it.

sections.label: Public servants voicing concerns
sections.summary: The passage says it must be made easier for public servants to voice concerns and that their concerns must be followed up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If you don’t care, nothing matters, so you are never upset".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to make sure that, one, we make it easier for public servants to voice their concerns and, two, make sure that we follow up on the concerns they raise.

sections.label: Internal Quality Service Managers
sections.summary: It suggests internal Quality Service Managers in Ministries and Statutory Boards to follow up on public servants' feedback and close the loop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This should also be made available to all public servants, not just in some Ministries or Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also suggest that we have an internal Quality Service Manager (QSM) within Ministries and Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They focus on external feedback from members of the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I suggest we put in place internal QSMs to follow up on feedback given by public servants and, similar to how we handle public feedback, they ensure that the feedback is looked into and the loop is closed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They will help give our public servants a voice and ensure that their views, feedback and suggestions are looked into so that the Public Service is strengthened.

sections.label: MOH aged-care policy ownership
sections.summary: MOH will take on policy ownership of aged-care services across the health and social domains from April this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MOH will take on policy ownership of the spectrum of aged-care services across both the health and social domains from April this year.

sections.label: MSF transfers SCN functions
sections.summary: MSF will transfer its Senior Cluster Network functions, including Senior Activity Centres and Cluster Support, to MOH.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MSF will transfer its functions under the Senior Cluster Network (SCN), which include the policies and planning of Senior Activity Centres (SACs), Cluster Support and Caring Assistance from Neighbours (CAN), Carers and other programmes, such as befriending services, to MOH.

sections.label: SLAS examined 250 seniors
sections.summary: The Singapore Longitudinal Ageing Studies by NUS examined 250 seniors above 65.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Singapore Longitudinal Ageing Studies (SLAS) by NUS examined 250 seniors above 65.

sections.label: SLAS frailty findings
sections.summary: SLAS followed 3,000 residents aged 55 and above and found lower-income, single, uneducated older adults tend to suffer physical frailty.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: SLAS followed 3,000 Singaporean residents aged 55 and above and found that older adults from lower-income groups, who are single and have no formal education, tend to suffer from physical frailty.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And 41.1% of the frail subjects lived in 1- or 2-room public housing.

sections.label: Community Networks for Seniors
sections.summary: Speaker welcomes Finance Minister's plan for Community Networks for Seniors nationwide by 2020, piloted in 2016 to connect stakeholders supporting seniors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Occasionally, sprucing up or eradicating bed bugs from their homes by volunteers can help in home-care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am very glad that the Finance Minister has mentioned setting up Community Networks for Seniors (CNS) programmes nationwide by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: CNS was piloted in 2016 with the aim of connecting different stakeholders in a community to jointly engage and support our seniors.

sections.label: AIC as central agency
sections.summary: Finance Minister said the Agency for Integrated Care will be the central implementation agency reaching seniors and caregivers and coordinating social and health services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance also said that the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) will be the central implementation agency to reach out to seniors and their caregivers as well as coordinate the social and health-related services to them.

sections.label: Ageing Gracefully@Home programme
sections.summary: Heng Swee Keat launched Ageing Gracefully@Home at Chin Swee in 2014, with Temasek Care supporting three years and AIC since then.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Mr Heng Swee Keat launched Ageing Gracefully@Home (AGH) programme at Chin Swee in 2014 − I notice that the Finance Minister is nodding, that means you remember, thank you − with Temasek Care supporting it for three years and AIC since then.

sections.label: Business costs and premises rental
sections.summary: Speaker says extending the Wage Credit Scheme addresses manpower costs, and suggests financial help for businesses, especially SMEs, to lessen premises rental burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The move to extend the Wage Credit Scheme (WCS) and all other related initiatives in continuation of support to firms in coping with near-term costs is rightfully addressed as they are directly linked to manpower, for example, Foreign Worker Levy (FWL), which is one of the major components of business operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I thought one component which is as critical, if not even more so, is premises rental.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we know, two major components of business costs in Singapore are manpower cost and premises rental cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These two will take up at least 50% of any business operation costs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, Mr Speaker, I would like to suggest on any form of financial help to be formulated for business operators, especially the small and medium enterprises (SMEs), to lessen their burden due to premises rental.

sections.label: Sharing the budget surplus
sections.summary: Speaker finds the $9.6 billion surplus surprising, calls saving part of it right, but thinks sharing $700 million, 7% of the total, is on the lower side.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The surplus of $9.6 billion accumulated in our financial year 2017 is very surprising to me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Henceforth, the decision to save part of the surplus for savings ahead is a right move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the sharing of $700 million with Singaporeans, which only accounts for 7% of the total $9.6 billion, I thought that is on the lower side.

sections.label: Financing major infrastructural projects
sections.summary: Speaker says what struck him about Budget 2018 is the fundamental change in how major and infrastructural projects will be financed in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What struck me about Budget 2018 is the fundamental change in the way how major and infrastructural projects are to be financed in future.

sections.label: China consumer segment growth
sections.summary: Statistics show China's consumer segment will grow from 50 million to 300 million people in coming years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the moment, statistics show that the consumer segment in China will grow from 50 million people to 300 million in the coming years.

sections.label: Malay community learning Chinese language
sections.summary: The speaker suggests young Malays learn Chinese and asks whether MENDAKI can offer Chinese language classes and sessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I suggest that our people, including the Malay community, pay close attention towards this development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I suggest that our young Malays be exposed to and learn to master the Chinese language.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Council for the Development of the Singapore Malay/Muslim Community (MENDAKI) take steps to offer classes and sessions that teach the Chinese language?

sections.label: Support for inclusive progressive Budget
sections.summary: The speaker says there is room for improvement but calls the Budget inclusive and progressive and supports it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While I opine that there is still room for further improvements, I believe it is a Budget which is inclusive and progressive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the points I have highlighted, I support the Budget.

sections.label: Budget 2018 foundation and shifts
sections.summary: Minister Heng Swee Keat said Budget 2018 lays the foundation for the next decade and outlined three major shifts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I was very happy that Minister Heng Swee Keat clearly stated that Budget 2018 is about laying the foundation for our nation’s development in the next decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: He outlined the three major shifts which are confronting us: the shift in global economic weight towards Asia, accompanied by broader shifts in the global order; emergence of new technologies; and our ageing population.

sections.label: Singapore as innovation node
sections.summary: Budget 2018's strategy is to anchor Singapore as a node for innovation, technology and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
