sentences.text: Budget 2018's strategy is to anchor Singapore as a node for innovation, technology and enterprise.

sections.label: Open Innovation Platform pilot
sections.summary: The Open Innovation Platform pilot will encourage co-creation of digital solutions via a virtual crowdsourcing platform for companies seeking partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Additionally, the pilot of the Open Innovation Platform will also encourage the co-creation of digital solutions by providing that virtual crowdsourcing platform to help companies find partners to address specific challenges they face.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and ASEAN talent
sections.summary: The passage says change is fast, doing it alone is untenable, and notes SkillsFuture's focus on Asia-ready and ASEAN talent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But more important is speed, because the pace of change is happening so quickly and continuously that trying to do it ourselves is not going to be tenable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: There have been many measures but I was glad to see the focus, even for SkillsFuture, on areas of developing talent for being Asia-ready and developing talent for us to be able to compete and engage in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) region.

sections.label: Mixing young and older workers
sections.summary: The passage states that combining younger and older employees lets companies use new perspectives and older workers' experience for a more effective workplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Because it is also the "how do you work together".

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: That is the important piece and I really firmly believe that our more mature workers today have a wealth of experience and knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: By bringing together a diverse workforce of both young and older employees, companies can tap on these new perspectives and the skills of their younger workforce and the wealth of knowledge and experience of older workers for a more effective work environment.

sections.label: Financial education in polytechnics and ITEs
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for more information on the planned financial education curriculum for polytechnic and ITE youths and why junior colleges are excluded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share more information on the financial education curriculum that is planned for our youths in our polytechnics and ITEs?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Is there a reason why the junior colleges are not included?

sections.label: GST increase effects questioned
sections.summary: The passage cites 2007 CPI inflation after the GST rise and asks how a 7% to 9% GST increase affects competitiveness, investment, tourism, MICE, CPI and inflation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2007, when the GST was raised from 5% to 7%, consumer price index (CPI) inflation rose to 2.6% in July 2007 from 1.3% in June, reflecting the 2% GST hike.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How will the proposed GST increase from 7% to 9% affect Singapore’s competitiveness?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Will the increase deter foreign direct investments into Singapore and hurt our tourism and the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) industry?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How will the proposed GST increase impact our CPI and inflation when implemented?

sections.label: Choosing power provider
sections.summary: The passage states that from the middle of this year Singaporean households can choose which provider to buy power from.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On a related note, from the middle of this year, Singaporean households will be able to choose which provider to buy their power from.

sections.label: Thanking Government for payout
sections.summary: The passage thanks the Government and Mr Heng Swee Keat for an early $100 to $300 payout to eligible Singaporeans aged 21 and above.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On behalf of my residents, I would like to thank the Government, and especially Mr Heng Swee Keat, for giving an early ang pow of $100 to $300 to all eligible Singaporeans aged 21 and above.

sections.label: Extension of WCS
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Government's intention to extend WCS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Next, I am glad that the Government intends to extend WCS.

sections.label: No SkillsFuture credit top-up
sections.summary: Residents were disappointed that there was no enhancement or top-up in SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Lastly, with all the talk about SkillsFuture and upgrading, there was disappointment felt by my residents that there were no enhancement and no top-up in SkillsFuture credits.

sections.label: Ageing population and support ratio
sections.summary: Singaporeans aged 65 and above are expected to double from 440,000 in 2015 to 900,000 by 2030, with the old-age support ratio projected to fall to 2.1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The number of Singaporeans aged 65 and above is expected to double from 440,000 in 2015 to 900,000 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our citizen to old-age support ratio, that is, the ratio of citizens in the working ages to each elderly citizen, is projected to fall to 2.1 in 2030.

sections.label: IPS study on Reserves
sections.summary: An IPS study showed 40% of Singaporeans think the Government should tap the Reserves rather than raise tax, 34% hold the opposite view, and 41% believe each generation should be self-reliant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin): A recent study by the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) in January this year showed that while 40% of Singaporeans think that the Government should tap into the Reserves, and not increase tax, to cope with the social expenditure on an ageing population, 34% of Singaporeans hold the opposite view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Forty-one percent of respondents believe that each generation should be self-reliant and not rely on another generation.

sections.label: Reserves during financial crisis
sections.summary: The Reserves let the Government back a $150 billion bank deposit guarantee in 2008 and fund the $4 billion Jobs Credit Scheme and Special Risk-Sharing Initiative in 2009.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The advantages include affordable imported goods and the leeway to draw upon these savings in times of emergencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is important to remind ourselves and the younger generation that during the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, with our Reserves, the Government could back the $150 billion guarantee for all bank deposits here and, in 2009, funded the $4 billion Jobs Credit Scheme and Special Risk-Sharing Initiative.

sections.label: Property taxes and social expenditure
sections.summary: BSD, ABSD and ASSD help preserve capital while revenue funds social expenditure such as subsidies and HDB CPF grants, and the speaker asks the Minister about benefit returns for low- and middle-income groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Presently, there are other taxes, such as Buyer’s Stamp Duty (BSD), Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty (ABSD) and Additional Seller's Stamp Duty (ASSD), that will help us preserve our capital while allowing revenue to fund for social expenditure, such as the many different types of subsidy and special HDB CPF grants for our younger generation to buy HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On that note, may I ask the Minister if for every dollar paid by the low-income group, they will get $4 or more in benefit, in return?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Likewise, for every dollar spent by the middle-income group, they will get back $2 or more in benefit, in return.

sections.label: Three areas of concern
sections.summary: The results showed three areas of concern: future uncertainty, cost of living, and shrinking family support.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The results showed three areas of concern: one, future uncertainty – their jobs and Singapore's economy; two, cost of living; and three, shrinking family support.

sections.label: Economic restructuring and senior jobs
sections.summary: The passage asks Minister Heng for insights on economic restructuring and private sector partnerships, and whether more jobs were created for middle-age and senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Can Minister Heng provide more insights on how our economic restructuring efforts have been, and how we have been encouraging partnerships in the private sector?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Have more jobs been created in different sectors, particularly for those in the middle-age group to senior workers?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: From 500,000 seniors today to 900,000 by 2030, this is not an insignificant increase in a decade.

sections.label: Tripartite partnership and hiring shift
sections.summary: The passage states tripartite efforts are a necessary partnership, but jobs for middle-age and senior workers need a fundamental shift in hiring.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Tripartite efforts with the private and public sectors are a necessary partnership.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: However, beyond encouragement from the Government, jobs creation for middle-age and senior workers can never be effected without a fundamental shift in the hiring process.

sections.label: Workdays off for upgrading classes
sections.summary: The passage suggests the public and private sectors consider allocating workdays off for staff upgrading classes or customised in-company courses.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Apart from the various initiatives, like Place-and-Train, Adapt and Grow, that help some mid-career switchers or displaced workers, what more can be done?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I suggest that the public and private sectors consider allocating some workdays off for their staff to attend relevant upgrading classes, or for collaboration between companies and course providers to offer customised courses in modules within the companies or the same industry in order to benefit more workers.

sections.label: Converting medical leave to care leave
sections.summary: The passage proposes mandating that companies allow employees to convert unused medical leave to family care or eldercare leave.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, to mandate that companies allow employees to convert unused medical leave to family care leave or eldercare leave for their immediate family members.

sections.label: Sustaining development and building reserves
sections.summary: The passage asks how to sustain developments without burdening the next generation and says strong reserves should be built for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: How can we sustain the multifaceted developments without burdening the next generation?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Next, we will plan for our family’s future and work hard for it to create a better life.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Hence, we should uphold the same principle, work hard and build strong reserves for future generations.

sections.label: Wealth preservation for future generations
sections.summary: The passage argues that unless we preserve wealth for children and grandchildren, tapping the Reserves and current surplus will always be tempting.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Our forefathers did exactly that, and here we are today, enjoying the fruits of their labour.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: This is not a rhetorical question, but one that makes us think about the need for wealth preservation and beyond our entitlements.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Unless we are prepared to do this for our children and grandchildren, the urge to tap on the Reserves and current surplus will always be tempting.

sections.label: CPF contribution rates for older workers
sections.summary: The passage urges reviewing CPF contribution rates for workers above 55, noting cuts at 56 and proposing no cuts until at least 60.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On the subject of continued employment of older workers, I would urge the Government to review the CPF contribution rates for employees above 55 years old.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Currently, once a worker hits 56 years old, their employer CPF contribution is slashed from 17% to 13%, while their employee CPF contribution is cut from 20% to 13%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In total, there is a drastic cut of 11% in CPF contribution overall.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: That is a huge cut when you cross 55 to 56 years old.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would propose that the CPF contributions not be cut until much later, say, when they are at least 60 years old.

sections.label: Concerns over GST and income tax
sections.summary: The passage notes worries about possible GST and income tax increases, and that the last personal income tax rate increment took effect for year of assessment 2017.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many have been worried about possible increase of the GST, and an increase in personal or corporate income tax rates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am aware that the last increment in personal income tax rates came into effect for year of assessment 2017, where those whose assessable income is more than $320,000 are taxed at 22%.

sections.label: Comparing Hong Kong and Singapore income tax
sections.summary: The passage states Hong Kong's maximum personal income tax rate is 17% and suggests room to raise rates for higher income earners in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In Hong Kong, the maximum personal income tax rate is 17% and this is applicable to those whose assessable income is more than S$33,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I feel there is room to increase the personal income tax rates for higher income earners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For instance, those whose assessable income is more than $320,000 and up to $500,000, can be charged a personal income tax rate of 22%.

sections.label: Higher corporate tax for large firms
sections.summary: The passage proposes charging MNCs or large firms earning over $1 billion annually a corporate tax rate of 17.5% to 18%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For MNCs or large firms, especially those that are earning annual revenues of more than $1 billion annually, which are among the top 1,000 earning firms in Singapore, they can be charged a higher corporate tax rate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These MNCs or large firms that are earning in excess of $1 billion annually, can be charged a corporate tax rate of 17.5% to 18%.

sections.label: IPS study on social class divisions
sections.summary: The passage states an IPS study found Singapore's most acute social divisions were based on class, not race or religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In an Institute of Policy Studies’ (IPS') study on Social Capital in Singapore conducted in December last year, it was found that the most acute social divisions in Singapore were now based on class, and not on race or religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: National University of Singapore sociologist Vincent Chua, one of the study's researchers, noted that while Singapore has done “a pretty good job of fostering multiculturialism and mixing between ethnic groups, the next step now is to increase efforts to increase mixing between classes”.

sections.label: Workfare, PWM and self-help groups
sections.summary: Workfare, the Progressive Wage Model and self-help groups like MENDAKI, SINDA and CDAC provide support through schemes from financial assistance to learning programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Programmes, such as Workfare, the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) and self-help groups, such as the Council for the Development of the Singapore Malay/Muslim Community (MENDAKI), the Singapore Indian Development Association (SINDA) and the Chinese Development Assistance Council (CDAC) also provide support through a variety of schemes from financial assistance to learning enhancement programmes.

sections.label: One-room rental flat home
sections.summary: The speaker says home was a 1-room rental flat until Primary 3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Home, for me, was a 1-room rental flat until I was in Primary 3.

sections.label: Father's pride and class divide
sections.summary: The speaker describes the father's face on seeing the metal badge, and first experiencing the class divide in an elite school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The look on my father's face when he saw the metal badge on my shirt made the hard work worthwhile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But Mr Speaker, Sir, much like the findings in the IPS study, it was in this elite school that I first experienced the class divide.

sections.label: Parents and teachers support group
sections.summary: Parents and teachers form the core of a special support group essential to narrowing the class divide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Parents and teachers are a powerful combination, and they form the core of a special support group that is essential if we are to narrow the class divide.

sections.label: Team sports and class divide
sections.summary: Bridging the class divide requires Singaporeans working together so every low-income child has perseverance, confidence and resilience, with team sports helping narrow social division.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the end of the day, bridging a class divide can only truly happen if Singaporeans work together to ensure that every single child from a low-income family is equipped with the perseverance, confidence and resilience to succeed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Encouraging greater participation in team sports and team-building activities would help engender a sense of community and help narrow the social division.

sections.label: Collective citizen will needed
sections.summary: Building a just and equal society takes time and needs the collective will of Singapore citizens, not just Government leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singaporeans expect much of our Government in this pressing matter, and rightly so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But can we not also expect just as much, if not more, from our people?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Building a society based on justice and equality, to achieve happiness, prosperity and progress for our nation, will take time and involve more than just the leadership of the Singapore Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will need the entire collective will of the citizens of Singapore, with heart and backbone.

sections.label: Singapore income inequality and Gini
sections.summary: Singapore's 2017 Gini coefficient, income gaps and slower income growth for the bottom 15% are stated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our Gini coefficient in 2017 stood at 0.459 before Government transfers and 0.402 after transfers, which has improved from 2013.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If one looks at household income from work, in 2017, the household income for the top 10% is more than $13,000 per person per month while that for the 20th percentile at the lower end is about $1,000 per person per month, or 12 times more unequal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our national gross domestic product (GDP) per capita last year was nearly $80,000, which means that the national GDP, when averaged out per person, is $80,000 per person per year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, when we look at median income or the halfway point for households, the Department of Statistics' data shows that for 2017, the median income per household member was only $32,400 per year, based on a monthly median per person of about $2,700.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Department of Statistics' data on key household income trends indicated that in 2017, there was a slower pace of income growth for the bottom 15% of households, showing a widening income gap.

sections.label: Government longitudinal studies intention
sections.summary: In 2013 the Government told Parliament it intends to do longitudinal studies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2013, the Government told Parliament that it intends to do longitudinal studies.

sections.label: Higher MediShield Life deductibles for elderly
sections.summary: Annual deductibles are higher for those aged 80 and above than for those aged 80 and below.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the annual deductible for persons aged 80 and below is between $1,500 and $2,000, the annual deductible for those aged 80 and above is between $2,000 and $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thus, the most senior of our people, aged 81 and above, who have the least income and most health problems, have to foot bills up to this higher deductible before MediShield Life will kick in.

sections.label: Question on higher deductibles for elderly
sections.summary: The passage asks why deductibles are higher when older people generally have less financial ability to pay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Why are deductibles also higher when, in general, the older people have less financial ability to pay?

sections.label: Singapore digital transformation index and study
sections.summary: Singapore topped an Asian digital transformation index, but a 2017 study found only 34% of leaders had a full digital strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: A few months later, the inaugural Asian Digital Transformation Index found that Singapore was top among Asian countries, including South Korea, Japan, Taiwan and Hong Kong, for its ability to transform itself amid digital disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, a Microsoft Asia Digital Transformation Study published in April 2017 found that while 75% of Singapore business leaders believed that they needed to transform to a digital business to enable future growth, only 34% had a full digital strategy in place.

sections.label: Alibaba revenue increase 2016 to 2017
sections.summary: Between 2016 and 2017 Alibaba's revenue rose 56% to over US$22 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Between 2016 and 2017, in one single year, Alibaba enjoyed a stunning 56% increase in revenue to over US$22 billion.

sections.label: Taxi quality of service rules
sections.summary: Taxi companies face pressure because LTA requires at least 92% of phone taxi requests to be matched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is pleasing to the commuters, but it puts taxi companies in a tight spot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is because taxi companies are regulated by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) under its Quality of Service (QoS) framework, and one of the criteria to demonstrate good quality of service is that at least 92% of taxi requests made by commuters through the phone have to be matched with taxis.

sections.label: Rail Infrastructure Fund and network
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance set aside $5 billion for a Rail Infrastructure Fund, and MOT plans to double the rail network to 360 km by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Coming back to the transport industry, we note that the Minister for Finance has set aside $5 billion from the 2017 Budget surplus to set up a new Rail Infrastructure Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) is also planning to double the rail network length to 360 kilometres (km) by 2030.

sections.label: Joint ventures for train projects
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Government could require overseas firms in future train projects to form joint ventures with local companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Given our size and our market, we may not be able to nurture a local company to be as big as Bombardier overnight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, could the Government require overseas firms involved in future train projects to form joint ventures with our local companies?

sections.label: Fresh Start Housing Scheme
sections.summary: The Fresh Start Housing Scheme helps rental flat residents buy a new flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, there is the Fresh Start Housing Scheme that helps the rental flat residents to buy a new flat.

sections.label: Rental residents childcare co-payment
sections.summary: Rental flat residents qualify for the $3 co-payment for childcare centre fees because their household income is $1,500 and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If the income level is less than $2,500, which applies to all the rental flat residents because the criterion to qualify for the Housing and Development Board (HDB) Rental scheme is household income of $1,500 and below, so they are able to qualify for the $3 co-payment for the childcare centres' fee, which is very affordable.

sections.label: Family care gaps study
sections.summary: The passage asks what efforts Government has made to study families' longitudinal fate and what care arrangements exist for children of shift workers at night.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: My question was: what efforts have been made by the Government to study the longitudinal fate of families over time?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Also, there are some care gaps, for example, workers who work shifts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: What care arrangements can be made for the children at night?

sections.label: Seniors living alone and ageing
sections.summary: A longitudinal study is suggested, and Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat cited ageing as a major shift, with seniors living alone more than doubling to 47,400 between 2006 and 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: She was at first saying that the Government is not doing enough but now say that these are the schemes that are available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: But I also agree with her that we could do a longitudinal study and both can come together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In his Budget speech, Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat cited ageing as one of the three major shifts that we must prepare for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We are told that the number of seniors living alone more than doubled between 2006 and 2016 to 47,400.

sections.label: Enhanced Proximity Scheme grants
sections.summary: The enhanced Proximity Scheme grant gives singles $10,000 to buy a resale flat near their parents and $15,000 to live with them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As HDB flats in mature estates are usually more expensive, the enhancement of the Proximity Scheme grant will hopefully assist and persuade more families to live with or near their parents even in the mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am glad that singles who buy a resale public housing flat to live near their parents will now receive $10,000 under the enhanced grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The grant for singles buying a resale flat to live with their parents has also been increased to $15,000.

sections.label: Second FDW levy increase
sections.summary: The FDW levy for the second FDW employed without levy concession will rise from $265 to $450.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The FDW levy for the second FDW employed without levy concession will go up from $265 to $450.

sections.label: Singles Premium reduction for elderly
sections.summary: A premium reduction of up to $5,000 based on income and lease length upholds the Singles Premium rationale but reduces its impact for elderly poor singles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A premium reduction of, say, upwards to $5,000, based on their income levels and length of lease, upholds the rationale of the Singles Premium, but reduces its impact for our elderly poor singles who can then use their savings for their retirement.

sections.label: Elderly stress and FDW levy
sections.summary: Elderly Singaporeans or their caregivers may feel stressed out, and the Foreign Domestic Worker Levy will be raised from $265 to $450.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Otherwise, elderly Singaporeans or their caregivers may feel stressed out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We know that the Foreign Domestic Worker Levy will be raised from $265 to $450.

sections.label: Singles above 55 premium reduction
sections.summary: For singles above 55 buying 2-room flats with shorter leases for the first time, the Government should consider lowering the premium by income and leasehold, capped at $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For singles aged above 55 who are buying 2-room flats with shorter leases for the first time, the Government should consider lowering the premium according to the buyer’s income and the leasehold of the flat, with the reduction in premiums capped at $5,000.

sections.label: Maritime Transformation Programme launch
sections.summary: The Finance Minister said the Maritime Transformation Programme was launched to boost Singapore's maritime hub competitiveness, industry transformation and maritime R&D.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In his Budget Statement, the Finance Minister mentioned the launch of the Maritime Transformation Programme (MTP) to enhance the overall competitiveness of Singapore as a maritime hub, accelerate industry transformation and deepen maritime research and development (R&D) capabilities.

sections.label: Foreign worker levy deferral
sections.summary: Minister Heng said foreign worker levy increases for shipyards will be deferred for another year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Heng also mentioned that foreign worker levy increases for shipyards will be deferred for another year.

sections.label: Marine and offshore ITM
sections.summary: The marine and offshore engineering ITM launched on 22 February identified LNG and offshore renewables as growth areas, and Minister Iswaran said Keppel and Sembcorp Marine entered LNG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The ITM for marine and offshore engineering which is launched on 22 February has identified liquified natural gas (LNG) and offshore renewables as two growth areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Iswaran said that Keppel and Sembcorp Marine have already ventured into the LNG segment.

sections.label: ASEAN Chair and disruptive economy
sections.summary: The Government can use its ASEAN Chair position to create cooperation opportunities with ASEAN companies, and the disruptive economy can affect maritime and offshore sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government can use its position as ASEAN Chair to help create opportunities for better cooperation with ASEAN companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My colleague, Leon Perera, spoke about disruptive economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We also cannot underestimate how the disruptive economy can affect what we do in the maritime and offshore sectors and bring changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It may not be sufficient fighting today's battle to stay ahead in the current competition by merely being more efficient, cheaper, faster and better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will we be able to ride the wave and think out of the box to create new relationships, opportunities, products, niche areas and new ways of doing business?

sections.label: Population above 65 by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, 27% of the population will be above 65 years old, meaning one in four persons will be over 65.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: By 2030, 27% of the population will be above 65 years old.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: One out of four persons will be over 65.

sections.label: Seniors Mobility and Enabling Fund top-up
sections.summary: The Finance Minister announced a $100-million top-up to the Seniors Mobility and Enabling Fund.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister has announced a $100-million top-up to the Seniors Mobility and Enabling Fund.

sections.label: BBC World Service report
sections.summary: A BBC World Service Report dated 20 February 2018 describes a democratically elected government that puts in a tax increase in four years' time.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: A British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) World Service Report dated 20 February 2018 put it this way: “Where else do you get a democratically elected government that puts a tax increase in, in four years' time? ….

sections.label: Budget 2018 road map
sections.summary: Budget 2018 spends less than it earns, proposes a GST increase in four years, builds Reserves, and the Finance Minister says it is a team effort backed by 4G Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: It gives us a road map on how to grow, given the challenges we face.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: It spends less than it earns and, where money may not be enough, it proposes an increase in GST, not now but in four years' time.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: And it continues to build up our Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: What Budget 2018 does not touch on is leadership succession.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, the Finance Minister has said in an interview with The Straits Times on 20 February that Budget 2018 is a team effort, involving the whole-of-Government.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: He has consulted the 4G Ministers who have backed the Budget, including the GST increase.

sections.label: Financial assistance for families
sections.summary: The MOE Financial Assistance Scheme will be reviewed to raise eligibility criteria, S&CC rebate extension will help household expenses, and the father could use Adapt and Grow schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, the Ministry of Education (MOE) Financial Assistance Scheme will be reviewed and one of the outcomes is that the eligibility criteria will be raised to cover more families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The father could also avail himself of the schemes within the Adapt and Grow programme and find a suitable job that will help to improve the family’s finances.

sections.label: Bukit Batok East school assistance
sections.summary: Families in Bukit Batok East sought help to buy school books and items, did not meet school criteria, appeals succeeded, and requests were referred to Giveaway Gateway.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: They did not meet the criteria to receive financial assistance from the schools and I had submitted appeals to the schools, which were eventually successful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I had also referred these requests to the Giveaway Gateway platform at Bukit Batok East, where the requests for assistance were conveyed to other residents.

sections.label: GST increase for long-term benefits
sections.summary: The Government must balance people's well-being with keeping the nation strong, so the GST rate must increase to achieve long-term benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Government needs to balance efforts to look after the well-being of the people, with the efforts to ensure that this nation stays strong for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must understand the need to increase the rate of GST to achieve long-term benefits.

sections.label: Global-Asia node quote
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance said Singapore must anchor itself as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise, and the Government has identified major international shifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Budget catches my attention for several reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But one thing that really jumps up at me was when the Minister for Finance said, and I quote, "We must anchor Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise, welcome investments, talent and ideas to Singapore, and be bold in venturing out into new markets." Sir, I believe that the Government has accurately identified the major international shifts that will change the world for our children.

sections.label: China-centred Asian capitalism
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore must transform its economy to stay useful in a new Asian capitalism centred on China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Global-Asia also means competitive pressures and realities, especially when the value chain of global production in the region diversifies even as the value chain reorients to centre on China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: China’s One Belt One Road Initiative expresses this, with the many lines of economic flow being re-imagined and reorganised as starting from China and extending in different directions westwards, southwards and northwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We have to make ourselves useful again in this new Asian capitalism centred on China by fundamentally transforming our economy.

sections.label: Mandarin and Global-Asia node
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with Lee Yi Shyan that learning Mandarin should be part of anchoring Singapore as a Global-Asia node.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But many people have observed that this kinship advantage is fading fast as China modernises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I agree with Lee Yi Shyan, Member for East Coast Group Representation Constituency (GRC), that the learning of Mandarin should be part of the overall strategy of anchoring Singapore as a Global-Asia node, as it will help us to connect to the 1.3 billion Chinese.

sections.label: Overseas Chinese concerns about China
sections.summary: Many overseas Chinese are concerned about China's intentions towards weaker states under one-party rule as a superpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They are excited that the so-called "Sick man of Asia" has now been fully awakened with the full force of 5,000 years of rich Chinese culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, Sir, many overseas Chinese are also concerned about the intention of China, especially under one-party rule and as a superpower, in her policy and attitude towards weaker states.

sections.label: China's impact on small states
sections.summary: The speaker is wary of China's political ambitions and worries Singapore could become a pawn in great power games.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How China behaves will have serious implications on small states in the region like Singapore in the near future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am personally wary of the political ambitions of China as a Global-Asia superpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am worried that Singapore, if we are not careful and if we fail in our economic strategy to become a Global-Asia node, would become a pawn on the chessboard of great power games in Southeast Asia.

sections.label: Budget vision and GST distraction
sections.summary: The speaker calls the Budget forward-looking but says the GST hike has become a distraction from its vision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is a forward-looking Budget to anchor Singapore firmly in the future and for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This has become an unnecessary distraction from the vision articulated in this Budget, and as a real distraction causing the Government to lose its focus in getting buy-in for the vision because it has to explain the future GST hike instead.

sections.label: GST hike for expenditure needs
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance announced raising GST in the foreseeable future to match increasing expenditure needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We will have to match these needs with the resources that are needed to do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And that is why the Minister for Finance has announced the need to raise GST in the foreseeable future to be able to match this increasing expenditure needs.

sections.label: Aviation and maritime industries
sections.summary: Aviation and maritime industries account for 10% of GDP and close to 170,000 jobs, with investments in Terminal 5 and Tuas Megaport.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our aviation and maritime industries today account for 10% of gross domestic product (GDP) and close to 170,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our mega investments in Changi Airport Terminal 5 and Tuas Megaport will continue to build on these strategic sectors.

sections.label: Government expenditures and value-for-money
sections.summary: Monies collected could have been left with citizens, and Government expenditures at 19% of GDP are prudent comparatively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Monies collected could have been left in our citizens' pockets, as their personal savings or for their own care for their families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I appreciate the value-for-money initiatives the Minister for Finance explained in his Budget Statement and acknowledge that, at 19% of GDP, our Government expenditures are prudent comparatively.

sections.label: Procurement certificate and lifecycle asset costs
sections.summary: DSTA and SUSS launched a procurement certificate, and asset purchases should be assessed via a lifecycle approach, especially long-lifecycle assets like lifts and rail parts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA) and the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) recently launched a certificate in procurement for public servants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Second, I would like to stress the importance of assessing asset purchases via a lifecycle approach so that costs are managed over the entire lifecycle of the asset.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is especially important when we look at assets that have a long lifecycle, like lifts and rail parts, which are intended to last 25 to 30 years.

sections.label: Support for Terminal 5 and Tuas
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Government's plans to invest in Changi Airport Terminal 5 and the Tuas Mega Port.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As such, I support the Government’s plans to invest in Changi Airport Terminal 5 and the Tuas Mega Port.

sections.label: Linking Singapore to innovation hubs
sections.summary: To seize opportunities in long-term trends, Singapore must link up with international innovation hubs, which is why the speaker supports the GIA programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To seize opportunities in the major long-term trends, we need to link Singapore up with international innovation hubs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is why I support the GIA programme.

sections.label: GST increase and global competition
sections.summary: In the face of global competition, Singapore must increase investment and embrace new trends, so the 2% GST increase does not need to come into effect this term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the face of increasing global competition, we must be bold enough to increase investment, embrace new trends and technologies and strive relentlessly to improve ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: That is why the GST increase of 2%, announced in the Budget Statement, does not need to come into effect during this term of Government.

sections.label: Income, expenditure and Reserves guarantee

sentences.text: Monthly income $5,000, monthly expenditure $5,500, result misery." On another note, Sir, I am most encouraged by our Government’s proposed innovative approach to using our country’s Reserves to guarantee loans for large-scale infrastructure projects.

sections.label: 900,000 seniors by 2030
sections.summary: The Minister's Budget Statement said Singapore will have 900,000 residents aged 65 and above by 2030, and the speaker commends the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: As the Minister said in his Budget Statement, by 2030, we will have 900,000 Singaporeans aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In closing, Mr Speaker, Sir, I commend the Minister for an integrated and strategic Budget which benefits Singaporeans and the economy of Singapore.

sections.label: 148 firms took up schemes
sections.summary: Only 148 firms took up assistance schemes designed to upgrade their firms and staff.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Only 148 firms took up assistance schemes designed to upgrade their firms and staff.

sections.label: SMEs, Wage Credit Scheme, carbon tax
sections.summary: It calls the trend unhealthy for SMEs, proposes extending the Wage Credit Scheme to bonuses, and supports a carbon tax for cleaner technologies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This trend is unhealthy as it affects the survival of our SMEs and results in wastage of resources through inefficient processes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I propose that the Wage Credit Scheme be extended to help SMEs retain staff by including performance and loyalty-based bonuses as part of the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As a global city with a compact built environment, it is crucial for all stakeholders of our society to adopt sustainable solutions to make Singapore an eco-friendly city.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I support the introduction of the carbon tax to encourage businesses to adopt cleaner technologies.

sections.label: Japan HEMS energy reduction study
sections.summary: The Energy Conservation Center Japan cites an 11% reduction in energy usage in facilities with HEMS after a 12-month study.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Energy Conservation Center Japan cites an 11% reduction in energy usage in facilities equipped with HEMS after a 12-month study.

sections.label: Kyoto incentivises eco-friendly organisations
sections.summary: Kyoto has tapped into its budget to incentivise schools, neighbourhood businesses and organisations to become eco-friendlier.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Two, Kyoto has tapped into its budget to incentivise schools, neighbourhood businesses and organisations to become eco-friendlier.

sections.label: Yokohama and Chiyoda green measures
sections.summary: Over 7,000 households took up a subsidy programme, Yokohama offers lower property taxes for energy-efficient houses, and Chiyoda assists buildings under its Greenstock Strategy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As of 2013, over 7,000 households have taken up the subsidy programme, making a seven-time increase over five years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Three, Yokohama provides economic incentives, such as lower property taxes for houses, if they meet certain energy-efficiency standards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Four, Chiyoda has developed measures for both new and existing buildings to become eco-friendlier and provide assistance in the form of technical support under its "Greenstock" Strategy.

sections.label: Pragmatic GST, NIRC, wealth tax decisions
sections.summary: Raising GST to 9%, not raising NIRC beyond 50%, and not implementing capital gains tax or more wealth taxes were each justified as pragmatic decisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The decision to raise GST taxes to 9% has been justified as a pragmatic decision in the face of growing national needs in the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And the decision to not raise our Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) beyond the 50% mark has also been justified as a pragmatic decision for the sake of signalling to currency markets the strength of our Singapore dollar.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And the decision to not implement capital gains tax or raise more wealth taxes as yet another alternative has also been justified as a pragmatic decision to maintain our attractiveness as a wealth management hub.

sections.label: Question on ideals versus pragmatism
sections.summary: The passage asks when it will be the right time to tilt the balance a little more towards ideals rather than always towards what is pragmatic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When will it ever be the right time to tilt our balance just a little more towards our ideals rather than always towards what is pragmatic?

sections.label: Reserves, NIR spending debate
sections.summary: The speaker opposes squandering Reserves, agrees using 100% of NIR is unwise, but cites Donald Low that 50% may not be right either, noting 60% would still add to principal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Every reasonable Singaporean believes in protecting our Reserves, and I am totally not supportive of any willful call to squander this once-in-a-lifetime inheritance on populist promises and things that would not last.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I agree with the Finance Minister's argument that using 100% of NIR is not a good idea because "the principal sum of Reserves will stagnate over time and the NIRC, as a share of GDP, will consequently fall as our economy grows".

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I can also appreciate economist Donald Low's perspective that "the current rule of spending only up to 50% of NIR means that the Reserves are still growing quite considerably every year… and just because 100% is not prudent does not mean 50% is right either." We would still be adding to the principal of the Reserves, even if it was at 60%.

sections.label: IMF reserves benchmark versus MAS reserves
sections.summary: The IMF considers adequate reserves to be 27% of GDP or S$113 billion, while MAS foreign exchange reserves alone are around S$369 billion or 88% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: IMF's opinion is that a good enough amount of reserves would be 27% of our GDP or S$113 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I do not know the size of our Reserves but I read that the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS') foreign exchange reserves alone are around S$369 billion or 88% of GDP.

sections.label: Income inequality, class divisions warning
sections.summary: A written reply warns that widening income inequalities could fracture society, and an IPS study found class may now be the sharpest social division.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In his written response to a Parliamentary Question this month, he said, "If we fail – if widening income inequalities result in a rigid and stratified social system, with each class ignoring the others or pursuing its interests at the expense of others – our politics will turn vicious, our society will fracture and our nation will wither." A recent Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) study on Social Capital in Singapore concluded that the sharpest social divisions here may no longer be race or religion, but class.

sections.label: PSC Chairman on young scholarship candidates
sections.summary: PSC Chairman Eddie Teo said yearly scholarship interviewees question Singapore's disparities and believe Government should do more for the poor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Chairman of the Public Service Commission (PSC), Eddie Teo, made a speech in 2015 where he shared his insights from his yearly interviews with the 350 young people vying for scholarships each year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He said of these potential future public sector leaders that they "think critically and question what is happening in Singapore…our socioeconomic disparities, our educational policy and system, and our political environment…And when they worry about social inequality and the lack of social mobility, some may have already moved away from one cardinal belief that our founding fathers had, that social welfare should be discouraged because it breeds a poor work ethic and a dependence on Government handouts….they believe that the Government should do more for the poor because they feel it is just." So, the young recognise the goodness of ad hoc help like SG Bonus, but they are also clear that such help is short-lived and unlikely to create deep satisfaction.

sections.label: Seven hundred million dollars alternative
sections.summary: Seven hundred million dollars could have gone to an MSF programme making a more significant, long-term difference.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Seven hundred million dollars is a substantial sum that could have gone into, say, a Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) programme that focuses on making a more significant, long-term difference.

sections.label: Divorced mother on cleaner's salary
sections.summary: After divorce, her mother raised her and her brother on a cleaner's salary under $1,000, mostly spent on two-room flat rental.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Her parents divorced and her mother had to take care of her and her brother on a cleaner's salary of less than $1,000, the bulk of which went into paying rental for a two-room flat.

sections.label: Girl seeking university funding
sections.summary: A girl now seeking university funding is held up for her achievement, her mother's, and the system's role.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This girl is amazing, she is phenomenal and she is now looking for a way to fund her university studies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I share her story to have us first consider, not just her amazing achievement but her mom's achievement as well as an individual beating the odds, but second, I would have us to consider all the multiple points in her story where we would have wanted to know whether the system did come alongside to aid this mother and child's heroic journey.

sections.label: Believing in children's potential
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether more children could have such stories if given systemic state support and belief.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can we believe there are actually more children out there who are capable of having a story like hers if we choose to believe in them and invest more systemic state support to care for parents and children who do not quite fit into our checkboxes of assumed indicators of future success?

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Do we believe that the child growing up in the worst circumstances has just as much to offer our country as the child who grew up in the best?

sections.label: Housing, education, rising to power
sections.summary: The speaker says these children and mothers are part of the 'We' and should get housing, education and chances to rise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They are all our children and they and their mothers are part of the "We" that we are pledged to serve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, give them the housing and the education and the possibility of rising into positions of power so that they, too, can play their part in our country's success story.

sections.label: Social development spending overdue
sections.summary: From the social service sector's perspective, such social development spending is overdue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: From the perspective of the social service sector, such social development spending is overdue.

sections.label: Prudent spending and sector sustainability
sections.summary: The speaker agrees on prudence, advocates a sustainable social service sector generating its own revenue, and requests resources for capability-building rather than a black hole.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: But having said that, I agree with the hon Member that we need to be prudent in our spending.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: Hence, I again advocate for the need for the social service sector to be sustainable, to generate their own revenue without compromising their mission to serve the disadvantaged and the vulnerable, to reduce their reliance on public funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: So, I still request for resources, but not to be invested into a black hole.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: I request for resources to invest in capability-building to achieve sustainability in the long term.

sections.label: Schools certify outdated competencies
sections.summary: Despite living in Industrial 4.0, schools continue to certify competencies relevant to earlier industrial economies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: Despite living in Industrial 4.0, our schools continue to certify competencies relevant to models of earlier industrial economies.

sections.summary: Schools, ITEs and IHLs should ensure every student knows machine basics, with differentiated routes for deeper learning and restructured courses allowing differentiated exits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: Schools, ITEs and IHLs should, therefore, ensure that every student knows some machine basics, with differentiated routes for deeper learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: In addition, courses, in general, may be restructured to allow differentiated exits into other courses, just as we currently allow differentiated entries into schools, institutions of learning and courses.

sections.label: Full-day schools level playing field
sections.summary: Allocating time and resources for push frontier practicals and converting schools to full-day sessions enables levelling the playing field among students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: With time and resources allocated for push frontier practicals, housing push frontier environment in school and converting schools to full-day sessions, have another advantage: it enables the levelling of the playing field among students.

sections.label: Full-day school reduces inequity

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: A full-day school can be a good tool to eliminate a part of that inequity.

sections.label: Knowledge transfer and KPIs
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to consider requiring Employment and S Pass holders to train staff, and to implement a systematic, evaluated system of knowledge and skills transfer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: In addition to the Capability Transfer Programme, perhaps whether the Government also consider that Employment and S Pass holders may be required to train those under their reporting lines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: Despite our success in the five decades, it could be timely for us to review our policies so that foreign companies which set up businesses in Singapore to take advantage of the various financial privileges and incentives, will leave an enduring legacy and enduring positive impact when they cease to operate in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider implementing a systematic, targeted, evaluated system to transfer knowledge and skills to Singaporean businesses and workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: Key performance indicators (KPIs) of officers should, therefore, not be how many partnerships have been forged, but how the terms of such partnerships have been negotiated to achieve win-win for both parties, as well as the impact of implementation of such terms.

sections.label: Measurables for local hires
sections.summary: Measurables could include increases in local hires for higher positions and in local employees trained and promoted from year zero and year-on-year.

sentences.text: Measurables could include an increase in local hires for higher positions, an increase in the number of local employees trained and promoted from year zero, and year-on-year.

sections.label: IMF reserve adequacy guidance note

sentences.text: Many Singaporeans are unhappy with the move to raise GST by 2% sometime between 2021 and 2025.
