sentences.text: Now, with better coordination among Government Ministries, the process has become smoother and faster, and our senior citizens’ problems can be resolved quickly.

sections.label: Policies for rapid ageing
sections.summary: The passage states that with Singapore undergoing rapid ageing, the right policies, resources and organisation should be set sooner than later.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: With Singapore undergoing rapid ageing, it is important that we set the right policies, put in the right resources and organise ourselves the right way sooner than later.

sections.label: Integrating health and social care
sections.summary: The passage praises the Government's move to integrate health and social care for seniors under one agency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For a start, I laud the Government’s move to integrate health and social care for seniors under one agency.

sections.label: CNS pilot for seniors' services
sections.summary: The passage states that preliminary results of integrating services for seniors through the CNS pilot have been seen, and it will soon be implemented nation-wide.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: On the ground, we have seen preliminary results of integrating services for seniors through the CNS pilot, which will soon be implemented nation-wide.

sections.label: AIC help for agencies
sections.summary: Some agencies may lack resources or the right help, but with AIC's help the process is smoother, more coordinated and faster.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Moreover, some agencies may not have sufficient resources or provide the right type of help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Now, with AIC’s help, the process is much smoother, more coordinated and faster.

sections.label: EHA Care Line service
sections.summary: He was enrolled in the 24/7 Eastern Health Alliance Care Line service, which he can dial into when lonely at night.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In addition, he was enrolled in the 24/7 Eastern Health Alliance (EHA) Care Line service, which he can dial into when he feels lonely at night.

sections.label: Adapting work for senior workers
sections.summary: The Government can lead in testing how work environment, workflows, job role designs, compensation and benefits can be adapted and optimised for senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Government can take the lead in testing how work environment, workflows, job role designs and even compensation and benefits, such as health benefits, CPF contribution, and leave conversion can be adapted and optimised for senior workers.

sections.label: Technology and AI in care
sections.summary: Leveraging technology and AI more effectively can drastically change how care is provided and help more Singaporeans age in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: By leveraging technology and AI more effectively, we can drastically change how care is provided and help even more Singaporeans to age in place.

sections.label: Second career for retirees
sections.summary: She will be happy if offered a career path to develop herself, so the Government should offer retirees a second career and career path.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: She will be very happy if she can be offered a career path, so that she can develop herself.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, I hope the Government offers retirees, like Mdm Morin Tan, a second career and develop a career path for them, just like any young applicant.

sections.label: IT systems for elderly rental units
sections.summary: Without using new-found skills they will forget them, so the Government should consider allocating financial resources to install simple IT or computer systems for the elderly in rental units.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But, without a chance to keep using their new-found skills, they will soon forget what they have learnt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Government to consider allocating financial resources to look into how we can install some form of IT or computer system for the elderly in our rental units, just like the installation of fire alarms in these homes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They do not need a desktop with a big gigabyte or a high-speed broadband, but just a simple screen, keyboard, mouse for them to also be “on-the-go”.

sections.label: Public engagement via interactive questions
sections.summary: The speaker suggests engaging the public through interactive questions, as done in the National Geographic programme "Do or Die".

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: On this important topic of communication, I would like to suggest that one way to get the public engaged is to have interactive questions put forth to them, just as it is done in the National Geographic programme “Do or Die” episodes on cable TV.

sections.label: Elderly services and engagement hopes
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the move of senior-related social support services from MSF to MOH and hopes for consideration of suggestions on retirees, computers and TV engagement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I wrap up on a very hopeful note.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am pleased that my request last year for a continuum of service for the elderly will now be a reality with the move of senior-related social support services from MSF to the Ministry of Health (MOH) from April to streamline care for the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I had also recently asked for a review of the nomenclature for ElderShield in my Motion on Support for Senior Citizens speech at the last Parliament Sitting, and I am hopeful that this, too, could be done following their review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope my suggestions for a second career for retirees, the Silver Computer Scheme and the very engaging and interactive TV platform to engage our citizens will be given consideration.

sections.label: Budget 2018 world standards
sections.summary: By world standards, Singapore's Budget 2018 is growth-friendly, relevant, futuristic and prudent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: By world standards, Singapore's Budget 2018 is growth-friendly, relevant, futuristic and prudent.

sections.label: Budget 2018 support measures
sections.summary: Budget 2018 supports employers giving wage increases, gives more financial support to lower- and middle-income students, continues rebate schemes, promises a permanent GST rebate and shares $700 million of surplus.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It not only supports employers who give wage increases to Singaporeans; it provides greater financial support to students from lower- and middle-income families through higher Edusave and financial and meals programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It continues with the various rebate schemes for household expenditure, promises a permanent GST rebate scheme and shares $700 million of last year's Budget surplus with every citizen.

sections.label: Budget 2018 GST hike and measures
sections.summary: Budget 2018 announced a 2% GST hike and includes measures like the Proximity Housing grant, Carbon Tax and raised CDC caps and matching grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The team behind Budget 2018 took courage by announcing the 2% GST hike, creating what some analysts call a constant "thorn" in the side of the ruling Government, for the next several years to come.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As a better-than-good budget, Budget 2018 incorporates, too, measures that align behaviours to the values that our society wishes to promote: the Proximity Housing grant, for instance, to encourage more family members to live with or near one another; the Carbon Tax, for instance, in support of the global and national movement to create a green and more liveable city; the raising of the cap and matching grants to the five CDCs so that they can raise more funds to meet gaps in the local district and support more assist, bond and connect initiatives.

sections.label: Fear hindering public service innovation
sections.summary: The speaker suspects fear of criticism, mistakes, failure, judgment and the AGC's "name and shame" list hinders innovation in the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In my years as an MP, I suspect the key hindrance to fostering more pervasive innovation in the Public Service is a four-letter word "FEAR" – fear of criticism by the public, by online critics, by even Members of this House from both the ruling party or otherwise; fear of making mistakes, fear of failing, fear of being judged and punished; or even fear of making it to the Auditor-General's Office's (AGC's) annual "name and shame" list of agencies and staff who are less than perfect.

sections.label: Culture of innovation in Singapore
sections.summary: MP asks the Minister how resources can be allocated to analyse why a culture of innovation is not pervasive in Singapore society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But if we do not settle this issue and find that balance, then we will continue to say that we want innovation in our society, in our country but, unknowingly, through our mindsets, actions, systems and processes, reward those who play safe and not try anything new nor rock the boat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, seek the Minister's views on how we can allocate some resources to analyse the root causes of why a culture of innovation is not pervasive in the various segments of the Singapore society.

sections.label: Smart city non-physical assets
sections.summary: MP asks what non-physical assets, especially in digitalisation, Singapore is investing in and creating to be a Smart city and nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If Singapore aspires to be a Smart city and nation, playing big not just in our own country but in the region or world-wide, what non-physical assets, especially in digitalisation, are we investing in and creating?

sections.label: Non-physical infrastructure investment balance
sections.summary: MP seeks the Minister's views on balancing investment in non-physical infrastructure assets and exporting Government capabilities and solutions for national revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I know, for instance, of good work done by MOE and the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) in education, such as learning management systems, that I see have the potential to go beyond internal consumption, or even healthcare solutions, for that matter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, seek the views of the Minister on how more balance can be granted to the development or investment in non-physical infrastructure assets and how good Government capabilities and solutions can be developed for export as one of the sources for our national revenue.

sections.label: Task force for vulnerable jobseekers
sections.summary: MP asks the Minister to consider setting up a task force within CFE to seek job opportunities for vulnerable and lowly-skilled Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In the context of the Singapore economy, as opportunities abound due to technology, due to the rise of the Asian/ASEAN economies, how do we ensure that each Singaporean has a boat to ride the tide with?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, seek the Minister to consider if a task force or a workgroup can be set up within CFE to specifically seek job opportunities for the vulnerable, the lowly-skilled elderly, the disabled and those who are not as endowed, those who are at risk or vulnerable, so that they will not be left behind, so that they do not simply just become welfare recipients.

sections.label: Donating SG Bonus to charities
sections.summary: MP seeks the Minister to give Singaporeans a choice to donate their SG Bonus to favourite charities before it is credited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, let us bring out the best in Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I seek the Minister to give Singaporeans a choice to donate their SG "hongbao" (the bonus) to their favourite charities, before the SG Bonus is credited to citizens.

sections.label: Fund for serving in ASEAN
sections.summary: MP says Singapore, as ASEAN chair, should look into setting up a fund to encourage Singaporeans to serve others in ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Singapore, as the chair of ASEAN this year, beyond the regional digitalisation plan that Deputy Prime Minister Tharman spoke about in the IMF meeting this week, should look into setting up a fund to encourage Singaporeans to go serve others in ASEAN.

sections.label: CDC funding and ENOUGH TALK
sections.summary: The Minister increased the funding cap so the Government matches CDC donations, and Central Singapore CDC started ENOUGH TALK to encourage action on issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: My fellow Mayors and I are thankful that the Minister had paid some attention to the CDCs and increased the funding cap so that the Government will match grants for donations that the CDCs are able to raise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In Central Singapore CDC where I serve, we started a series called ENOUGH TALK to encourage people to not just criticise but take action on issues that they care about, such as the low-skilled elderly who might be doing very manual difficult work at the hawker centres and toilets, and the cardboard collectors, the homeless, the hungry; and such as urging Singapore to support climate action by simply going "plastic-light" or finding ways to reduce styrofoam plates and boxes used at the many buffets and food distribution charity activities for the needy.

sections.label: Enrichment classes for lower-income children
sections.summary: CDCs and SG Cares encourage Singaporeans to help lower-income children get enrichment classes and holiday opportunities equal to their peers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Good enrichment classes for children from lower-income families so that they, too, have equal access to opportunities and holiday enrichment opportunities like their peers from the more affluent families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Therefore, the CDCs and other members of the SG Cares movement encourage Singaporeans to join us to help our neighbours grow good crop.

sections.label: Giving and post-Budget discussions
sections.summary: The team sought views before the Budget and prepared communications materials so Singaporeans can comprehend and partake in post-Budget discussions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: So, Singapore, do give in order to become wealthier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I know the team had put in tremendous efforts seeking views, way before the Budget was stitched, and mulled over the many options and even spent much time preparing communications materials so that Singaporeans will comprehend and partake in the post-Budget discussions.

sections.label: Integrated plan and senior care services
sections.summary: Minister Heng asked the Government to accept an integrated plan, and senior care services will be led by MOH to be planned and delivered holistically.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, among other things, Minister Heng has asked the Government to accept an "integrated" plan, one that could pool together resources and pool efforts across stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am delighted, for example, that senior care services will be led by a single Ministry, MOH, to "enable these services to be planned and delivered holistically", an eminently sensible first step, Mr Deputy Speaker, as those of us who are caregivers to elderly parents and relatives will acknowledge.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The face of a caregiver is usually seen through a child.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But increasingly, given that one in four Singaporeans by the year 2030, as we know, is going to be above the age of 65, and soon many of us will not just have elderly parents or grandparents, we will also have extended families who deserve and need urgent medical care but increasingly financial assistance.

sections.label: Elderly couple and reverse mortgages
sections.summary: An elderly couple above 85 asked what happens if they live beyond the 15 years promised in their last lease.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They have an MP whom they greatly respect and admire whom I shall not name, in case I am playing favourites.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But what I will say is that after numerous visits to the HDB office to talk about how to talk about reverse mortgages and a sell-back package which are both financially beneficial for them in the next years in their twilight years – they are both above the age of 85 – there is one question that breaks the heart, and that question is when they asked a grand nephew: "What happens if I live beyond the 15 years that have been promised in my last lease I can take?" It is especially hard and tough to swallow because this is the third house they have gone through because of rightsizing.

sections.label: Question on tightening purse strings
sections.summary: A repeated question with this year's Budget Statement is why the purse strings are being tightened now, since Singapore has done remarkably well.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When I speak to my fellow Singaporean friends, colleagues, a question that has emerged with this year’s Budget Statement and which has been repeated time and time again is: "Why are we tightening the purse strings now?" This is a natural question, Mr Deputy Speaker, because we have done so remarkably well this financial year.

sections.label: Communicating corporate ethic to Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Budget's corporate work ethic message will reach everyday Singaporeans facing direct taxation from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He does not use these words, but it is inherent in the Budget speech that there should be this corporate work ethic and innovation that should be infused within Government-owned infrastructure companies, for example, Government agencies, to ensure that, very much like how private companies fund acquisition and expansion, so should our Statutory Boards and infrastructure companies.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I do ask this: how will this message be communicated from this point onwards to the non-professionals, to the non-business people, to everyday Singaporeans who would have to deal with the direct taxation that will be coming in 2021 to 2025?

sections.label: GST raised beyond 2021
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether GST could be raised beyond 2021 if new gaps emerge despite prudent spending and the save and borrow scheme.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is there a real likelihood, many have asked me, on the current projections as to whether GST could be further raised beyond 2021 if, despite prudent spending and the "save and borrow" scheme and the policy we have for infrastructure projects, new gaps emerge?

sections.label: National corporate social responsibility plan
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes corporate giving and asks the Ministry to consider a national action plan on corporate social responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just as Singaporeans are asked to give back to society, I, therefore, welcome initiatives that encourage corporate giving.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I would ask that beyond the Business and Institutions of a Public Character (BIPC) Partnership Scheme, the Ministry could consider a national action plan on corporate social responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To prosper over time, corporations should not only deliver financial performance but should also see how they could make a positive societal contribution.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just as the Public Service in Singapore is being encouraged to adopt, as I have mentioned earlier, a corporate ethic and culture to "do well", corporations, too, should be encouraged, Mr Deputy Speaker, or perhaps even required, to adopt the core culture of the Public Service, that is, an unstinting commitment to "do good" in the public interest.

sections.label: GST offset and Budget support measures
sections.summary: The GST increase will be eased for lower-income families through increased GST Vouchers and offset packages, with added healthcare, education and business support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As regards the left, the increase in GST will be implemented in a way that tries to ease the extra burden on lower-income families ‒ the permanent GST Voucher scheme will be increased and offset packages will help families adjust to the increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Budget also looks to render more support for healthcare and education by having more meal coverage for secondary school students under the Schools Meal Programme and increasing the merit bursary quantum for pre-university students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There is also a review on subsidising premiums to ElderShield for the lower- and middle-income to keep healthcare affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Indeed, this Budget continues to subsidise business costs, employers and business owners through the continuation of the Wage Credit Scheme, the enhanced and extended Corporate Income Tax Rebate, and the Productivity Solutions Grant.

sections.label: Growth in MOH healthcare budget
sections.summary: The MOH budget grew from $4 billion in 2010 to $10 billion this year, and at least $13 billion from 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: One, healthcare for all Singaporeans, including those who helped to build Singapore, the budget for MOH has grown from $4 billion in 2010 to $10 billion this year, to "at least" $13 billion from 2020.

sections.label: Security spending by MHA, Mindef, MFA
sections.summary: Security spending by MHA, Mindef and MFA rose from $14.8 billion in 2010 to $19.5 billion in 2016, about a quarter of the national Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2010, spending by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), the Ministry of Defence (Mindef) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) on security was $14.8 billion and it has since increased to $19.5 billion, or 32%, on security in 2016, amounting to about a quarter of the national Budget.

sections.label: Preschool sector spending 2020
sections.summary: By 2020, spending on the preschool sector will be $1.7 billion per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By 2020, spending on the preschool sector will be at $1.7 billion per year.

sections.label: Land sales revenue proposal
sections.summary: The 20% land sales suggestion and 20-year average do not solve the issue because land sales revenue fluctuates and the average can be pushed upward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The suggestion on 20% of land sales for that year does not solve that issue; neither would value of average land sales over 20 years resolve that issue as, one, land sales revenue can fluctuate over a long period of time; and two, even if it is pegged to the average land sales over 20 years, this average can be pushed upward each year to more and more sales.

sections.label: Reversionary lease and Reserves
sections.summary: The reversionary lease returns to the Government only later while income is spent now, so land sales revenue should be treated as Reserves and invested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The point is not that the reversionary lease returns to the Government but that the reversionary lease only returns to the Government 100 years later or 10 years later and you would have spent the income from the sales this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This does not lend itself to financial prudence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is better to treat revenue generated from land sales as Reserves, invest it and use the net income from it up to 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: When the Government projects far into the future and takes decisive fiscal action now, we win as a state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: On the basis that we are called to be stewards in this House, I support the Budget.

sections.label: Budget anchoring Singapore
sections.summary: The most important part of this Budget is anchoring Singapore, and GST is not part of this Budget's measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: I thought the most important part of this Budget is anchoring Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: I am not saying that revenue is not important, but GST is not part of the Budget measures at this Budget.

sections.label: Alternatives to raising GST
sections.summary: They question whether there is any other avenue to look at instead of raising GST because it affects a lot of people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: What we are saying, and we are questioning whether or not, is there any other avenue to look at instead of raising GST because it affects a lot of people.

sections.label: Announcing GST increase timing
sections.summary: It is good to announce beforehand, but the question is whether it must be announced with this Budget, and the increase comes after the next election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: It is good to announce it beforehand but the question is whether you need to announce it together with this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: And I think Deputy Prime Minister Tharman promised that we have enough money to spend, we will not increase GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: The next election is 2020 or 2021, so you are going to increase it after the next election, good to announce it now.
